Two year contract (renewable) ORGANIZATION OVERVIEW Wellspring believes every child deserves an education that nurtures their full vibrant potential, and that children thrive when the whole school community rallies together to nurture and educate their children. OUR DREAM: A compassionate, creative, and courageous generation, shaping a vibrant and peaceful future. OUR PATH: We equip school communities to nurture children’s character, intellect, and wellbeing — helping children in Rwanda and East Africa to thrive. Wellspring is at an exciting and visionary stage in its journey. Established as a Canadian charitable organization and registered as an international NGO in Rwanda since 2008, Wellspring has over 20 years of credible experience supporting children’s education through the provision of training and coaching for teachers, leaders, parents, community members and teacher trainers across Rwanda. As an integrated global team with leadership now based in Rwanda, we are setting ourselves on course to establish Wellspring as a thriving and sought afterhub of educational expertise and professional development opportunities for educators in Rwanda and across East Africa, focussed on seeing children thrive with skills and knowledge for their wellbeing, character, resilience. JOB SUMMARY The Rwanda Partnerships Lead is a dynamic, strategic and creative new role within Wellspring’s team in Rwanda and plays a pivotal role in Wellspring’s strategic priority of rallying wider community support for children’s education and wellbeing, and raising awareness of Wellspring among an expanded external audience in Rwanda and into East Africa. This role serves as a key public-facing representative of Wellspring, working closely with the Executive Director to cultivate and manage relationships with strategic partners, corporates, foundations, donors, government stakeholders, churches, as well as educational partners, in collaboration with the Communications and PR Coordinator. Oversight, accountability and coaching will be provided by the International Director of Strategic Development and Partnerships in Canada. The Rwanda Partnerships Lead will be comfortable and confident with a range of stakeholders, responsible for identifying, nurturing, and stewarding philanthropic opportunities in the region; supporting grant proposals and reporting; strengthening partnerships; and advancing corporate giving and institutional engagement. This role plays a critical part in Wellspring’s long-term sustainability. Identify, scope, and cultivate philanthropic opportunities including individuals, corporates, foundations, trusts, and regional donors. Build and manage a regional donor and prospect pipeline, with clear cultivation and stewardship plans. Work closely with the Executive Director on high-level donor engagement and relationship management. Report to and collaborate with the International Director of Strategic Development and Partnerships to ensure regional fundraising integrates with global strategy and systems. Identify and engage potential corporate partners aligned with Wellspring’s mission and values. Develop tailored partnership concepts, proposals, and stewardship approaches in collaboration with Communications and Development teams. Manage and grow existing corporate relationships to ensure mutual value and long-term partnership. GRANTS, INSTITUTIONS & GOVERNMENT RELATIONS Research, cultivate, pursue and support grant opportunities from regional foundations, institutions, and international funders operating in East Africa. Collaborate closely as part of the global Development team on grant research, proposal development, and reporting. Support and strengthen relationships with government ministries, districts, and education authorities, including the development and management of MOUs. Represent Wellspring in relevant government, donor, and sector forums alongside the Executive Director. Contributing to grant reporting as part of a team, coordinating submissions or taking a lead writing role when required. PARTNERSHIP STRENGTHENING & MANAGEMENT Strengthen and steward existing, evolving and new partnerships with implementing partners, NGOs, education networks, and strategic collaborators. Support partnership design, implementation alignment, and ongoing relationship management. Represent Wellspring externally at meetings, events, conferences, and sector convenings to increase visibility, credibility, and influence. VISIBILITY AND EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT Working closely with the Communications & PR Coordinator, plan and oversee the implementation of public relations strategy to improve Wellspring’s brand awareness in Rwanda and contribute to advocacy initiatives. (required) Experience cultivating and stewarding relationships with partners and donors. (required) Experience with community-based NGOs or education-focused initiatives (desirable). Event coordination and management. title: Young Economist Program
raw_text: MINECOFIN/BNR Young Economist Program with GIZ support 9th Cohort – 2026/2027 Background The Young Economist Program (YEP) provides an excellent opportunity for aspiring young Rwandan economists and helps create a strong “recruitment pool” of highly qualified Economists who can take up professional and leadership positions in the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN), the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR), and other government ministries and agencies. The program seeks to bridge the gap between academia, the workplace, and policy analysis, while equipping young economists with a strong understanding of the role of public policy in sustainably improving the well-being of the population. The program is implemented by MINECOFIN and BNR with the support of GIZ Rwanda. Since 2016, eight cohorts have graduated, contributing to a growing pool of young economists serving across key public institutions, including MINECOFIN, BNR, the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA), and the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR). Notably, approximately 90% of staff in MINECOFIN’s Office of the Chief Economist are graduates of the previous eight cohorts. The program is now preparing for its ninth cohort. The YEP combines practical experience with structured learning and mentorship. Participants gain hands-on experience at MINECOFIN and BNR, benefit from mentorship and seminars delivered by national and international experts, complete relevant online and in-person courses, and prepare and present analytical briefs. Their professional conduct and performance are assessed throughout the program. The program targets highly qualified Rwandan economists aged 30 years or below who hold at least a bachelor’s degree in Economics, Development Economics, Macro-Fiscal Economics, International Trade/Economics, Monetary Economics, Econometrics, Statistics, or a related field. A master’s degree in one of these fields is considered an asset. About the YEP 9 The 2026/27 YEP equips Young Professionals with the skills and experience required to work across different economic departments of MINECOFIN and other ministries and government agencies. The program combines three main components: (a) a continuous internship with on-the-job training and mentoring; (b) intermittent formal group training in applied economics, quantitative methods, and relevant software/s; and (c) continuous self-study, including a research project at a later stage of the program. Progress and performance are assessed throughout the program through performance evaluations and written tests. Learning outcomes By the end of the program, participants are expected to have strengthened their competencies in three core areas: Applied economic analysis and problem-solving: Critically assess economic and policy issues and apply economic concepts and analytical approaches to policy questions arising in the day-to-day work of MINECOFIN and other public Economic institutions. Quantitative and data analysis: Apply quantitative methods and relevant software/s for macroeconomic projections, policy analysis, and assessing the impacts of policies and external developments on the economy and citizens’ well-being. title: Assistant Teacher Trainer - Inclusive Education
experience_raw: Entry level (1 to 3 years of experience)
raw_text: JOB OPPORTUNITY Assistant teacher trainer-Inclusive Education Location: Kigali-Rwanda Contract:One year renewable ABOUT THE MOYO CENTER The Moyo Center is a Rwanda-based organization working to strengthen inclusive education through teacher training, professional development, research, curriculum development, and community building. Our goal is to help create educational environments where children with disabilities, including children with autism and other learning and developmental differences, can meaningfully learn, participate, and thrive. THE OPPORTUNITY We are looking for an enthusiastic, practical, and growth-minded Assistant Teacher Trainer – Inclusive Education to join our team. The successful candidate will work closely with our Senior Teacher Trainers to co-facilitate professional development, assist in school coaching, support demonstration classrooms, and help design practical learning materials for partner schools. This role is ideal for an educator with strong classroom experience or early experience in teacher support who is eager to build their skills in adult training, coaching, and inclusive curriculum development. PURPOSE OF THE ROLE The Assistant Teacher Trainer will support the planning and delivery of training programs that equip teachers with the skills to support learners with diverse needs. The role involves co-facilitating workshops, assisting with classroom observations and follow-ups, supporting resource creation, and contributing to a continuous learning model across partner schools. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Training Assistance & Co-Facilitation Assist in preparing and co-delivering interactive, practical training sessions for teachers and school staff. Help set up and facilitate workshops, small group discussions, hands-on activities, and classroom simulations. Support the gathering of participant feedback and assist in adapting materials to meet teacher needs. 2. Inclusive Education Practice & Support Support teachers in implementing foundational inclusive strategies, including differentiated instruction, positive behavior support, classroom accommodations, and communication tools. Support strategies tailored for learners with autism, learning disabilities, and other developmental differences. 3. Coaching, Observation & Follow-Up Conduct follow-up visits to partner schools to observe classroom practice under the guidance of senior trainers. Provide constructive, encouragement-focused feedback to teachers. Help model effective inclusive techniques alongside classroom teachers. Assist in tracking teacher progress and identifying common classroom challenges. 4. Materials & Content Development Assist in drafting and organizing training presentations, handouts, visual aids, and low-cost classroom learning materials. Support the contextualization of inclusive education tools for the Rwandan school context. 5. Demonstration Classrooms & Documentation Assist in setting up and maintaining model inclusive classrooms. Help document success stories, lessons learned, and training data for monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) purposes. 6. Stakeholder Engagement Maintain positive, respectful relationships with teachers, school administrators, and families during school visits and training events. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE Required Rwandan nationality. Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Education, Special Needs Education, Inclusive Education, Psychology, or a related field At least 1 to 3 years of direct teaching experience or early experience assisting in teacher training/coaching. Basic understanding of child-centered learning and inclusive education principles. Good facilitation, presentation, and interpersonal skills. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Professional fluency in written and spoken English. Fluency in Kinyarwanda. Strongly Preferred Direct experience teaching or supporting learners with autism, intellectual disabilities, or special educational needs. Experience creating practical teaching aids or learning materials. Familiarity with Rwandan public school contexts and basic inclusive education guidelines. HOW TO APPLY Please submit the following documents to olivier@aeprogram.org: Updated CV / Resumé Cover letter detailing your experience and interest in inclusive education Contact details for two professional referees Email Subject: Application – Assistant Teacher Trainer – Inclusive EducationDeadline: 26th October, 2026 Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. The Moyo Center is committed to inclusion, equal opportunity, safeguarding, and creating a safe and respectful environment for all children, educators, and staff. Apply

title: Safeguarding Officer
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE (TORs) FOR RECRUITING SAFEGUARDING OFFICER FOR FAWE RWANDA CHAPTER 1.Background The Forum for African Women Educationalists (FAWE) is a membership-based Pan-African Non-Governmental Organization that operates through 34 National Chapters in 33 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa to promote girls’ and women’s education. FAWE’s vision, mission and goal focus on quality education for girls and women socio-economic empowerment. FAWE Rwanda is one of 33 national chapters. FAWE Rwanda Chapter was started in 1997 and since its inception, FAWE Rwanda has grown to become a reputable partner and focal point on female education in Rwanda. FAWE Rwanda Chapter would like to recruit Safeguarding Officer for a period of 3 years renewable upon the performance and resource availability. Job Title: Safeguarding Officer Job family: Technical Reports to: Executive Director Direct reports: None Job Purpose: The core purpose of the IT Officer is to provide secure, reliable and innovative ICT services that enable FAWE Rwanda's staff and programmes to operate effectively. The IT Officer will manage and support ICT infrastructure, digital systems, cybersecurity, data, IT assets and digital platforms. Provide technical support to projects and organizational initiatives, build staff digital capacity, and identify opportunities to leverage emerging technologies, automation and innovation to improve efficiency, programme delivery and organizational performance. 3. Major responsibilities: Performance Areas. Policy & Procedure Weight: 30% Maintain, propose review, and propose updates to the organization’s Safeguarding Policy at least annually, or sooner if legislation, guidance, or organizational context changes. Ensure safeguarding procedures are clearly documented, accessible, and understood by all staff and volunteers. Ensure the policy is compliant with relevant national child protection and vulnerable adult legislation and guidance. Organize annual safeguarding refresher training and periodic briefings on safeguarding responsibilities and emerging risks. Promote a culture in which staff, volunteers, and program participants feel confident raising concerns without fear of reprisal. Act as the organizations’ primary safeguarding liaison with partner organizations, donors, and regulators where relevant. Work closely with HR on the recruitment process by ensuring safeguarding-related aspects are included throughout the process. Reporting and Case Management Weight: 35% Act as the first point of contact for any safeguarding concern, disclosure, or allegation. Receive, log, and assess all safeguarding concerns using the organizations’ standard reporting form. Advise on the appropriate next steps for each concern received. Maintain a confidential, secure record-keeping system for all safeguarding concerns, actions taken, and outcomes. Refer to health, psychosocial, legal-aid and statutory child-protection or police services. Follow up on referred cases to ensure appropriate action has been taken. Report serious incidents to the Board of Directors, Senior Management or relevant governance body in a timely manner. Do not investigate a criminal allegation unless trained and designated as investigator, and never where the officer has a conflict of interest Maintain a secure, access-controlled record of concerns, actions and outcomes. Share information only with those who need it to protect, refer, investigate or meet a legal duty. Provide regular safeguarding reports at minimum, monthly to the Management or Board of Directors where required, summarizing concerns raised, trends, and actions taken, while preserving confidentiality of individuals involved. Offer survivor assistance in line with available services, whether or not there is an investigation, and do not make assistance conditional on the survivor supporting the case management process. Prevention, Training and Safe Programmes Weight: 25% Ensure every staff member and volunteer completes safeguarding induction before unsupervised contact with participants, and in any case within 30 days of engagement, and completes an annual refresher. Brief consultants and visitors who will be in contact with participants. Keep a record of who has been briefed. Maintain at least one reporting route that a program participant can use without passing through the adult who may have harmed them, and make that route known in schools, clubs and offices. Support programme risk assessments before scholarships, mentoring, residential activities, transport of children, school clubs, research and media work proceed. High residual risk is signed off by the Executive Director. Activity does not proceed if the risk cannot be managed. Apply the FAWE Africa Informed Consent Package to images, stories, research, and all program engagement with children and vulnerable adults. Refusal to consent or assent has no effect on access to a programme. Promote a culture in which staff, volunteers and program participants can raise concern without fear of reprisal. Retaliation is itself misconduct and is reported as a safeguarding concern. Assess a partner’s safeguarding capacity before FAWE Rwanda funds or jointly delivers with that partner. A partner that cannot meet the minimum needs a time-bound strengthening plan, or the partnership does not proceed. Ensure partner agreements require notification to FAWE Rwanda within 24 hours of an allegation of trafficking, exploitation or abuse linked to FAWE-funded programming or staff, or that could reasonably affect the relationship. Ensure suppliers sign the Supplier and Service Provider Code of Conduct once issued, and that consultants acknowledge the safeguarding policy in their contract. Resource mobilization Weight: 10% Participate in design of project proposals for future funding. Search and share prospective funders and funding opportunities for FAWE Rwanda programs. Representing FAWE Rwanda in technical program partnership forums when deemed necessary. Contribute to procurement processes and any other responsibilities related to the program. Other duties Ensure compliance with FAWE Rwanda Chapter policies and all relevant legislations. Act at all times according to FAWE Rwanda’s values and in support the achievement of its vision, mission and values. To undertake other duties of a similar nature as reasonably required by the line manager. 4. Person Specification Essential: Demonstrable understanding of safeguarding principles and child/vulnerable adult protection frameworks. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to handle sensitive information with discretion. Ability to remain calm and act decisively in emergencies or high-pressure situations. No safeguarding-related conduct concerns on record; willingness to undergo background/police clearance checks. 5. Person specifications Academic & professional qualifications At least a bachelor’s degree in any of the following disciplines awarded by an accredited university: Education, Human Resource Management, humanities, business administration or related social science. Post graduate qualification in any of the above disciplines is an added advantage. 6. Essential experience At least 7 (seven) years working experience in education system as teacher/lecturer, school administrator, counsellor, or similar roles. At least 5 (five) years previous field experience in a Non-Governmental Organization. Demonstrable experience in developing, implementing and embedding safeguarding and child protection policies and procedures. Knowledge of HR policies, procedures and processes. Proficient written and verbal communication skills in English. Good knowledge of MS Office Applications, and other ICT platforms, ability to learn quickly Be a person of integrity to handle confidential or sensitive information Ability to work with people from diverse background 7. Essential knowledge Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, French and Kinyarwanda. Proficiency in multimedia content creation and digital platforms. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

raw_text: Job Title: Plant Manager(Processing)Location: Kigali, Processing PlantReporting to: Aquaculture Operations Manager Contract Type: Full-time, on-site (shift-based operations) About Kivu Choice: Kivu Choice is Rwanda’s largest protein producer and one of the fastest-growing aquaculture companies in Africa. Founded in 2022, Kivu Choice is the sister company to Victory Farms, East Africa’s leading aquaculture platform based in Kenya. The company operates a fully vertically integrated aquaculture model, encompassing hatchery operations, cage-based grow-out, processing, distribution, and sales. Kivu Choice is also one of the country’s largest employers with over 700 employees, and plans to grow to 1,200 employees within the next three years, reflecting its strong commitment to job creation and inclusive economic development. Over the next five years, Kivu Choice aims to scale into Africa’s largest and most sustainable protein producer, producing and distributing 30,000 tons of fish annually for the Rwandan market and for export across the region. Job Purpose: The Plant Manager leads the day-to-day running of Kivu Choice’s fish processing plant, ensuring that machinery-heavy production lines run safely, efficiently, and without unplanned stoppages. The role owns process control, preventive and corrective maintenance, and quality and food safety compliance across the plant, while leading shift teams and operators. As Kivu Choice scales volumes toward 30,000 tons a year, this position is critical to protecting throughput, yield, and product quality from intake through to cold storage and dispatch. Key Responsibilities: 1. Production & Process Control Plan and run daily production to meet volume, yield, and quality targets across all processing lines. Set, monitor, and adjust process parameters (line speeds, temperatures, and processing times) to keep output consistent. Develop and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) for every line and piece of equipment. Identify bottlenecks and lead continuous improvement to raise throughput and reduce waste. Coordinate with harvest, logistics, and sales teams so that raw material intake matches plant capacity and orders. 2. Preventive & Corrective Maintenance Build and run a preventive maintenance schedule for all plant machinery, refrigeration, and utilities. Lead fast troubleshooting and corrective repairs to keep unplanned downtime to a minimum. Maintain equipment history, maintenance logs, and a critical spare parts inventory. Manage external technicians and suppliers for specialized servicing and repairs. Advise on equipment upgrades, new installations, and capacity expansion. 3. Quality Control & Food Safety Implement and maintain food safety systems in line with HACCP, GMP, and ISO 22000 principles. Monitor critical control points and ensure corrective action is taken and documented when limits are breached. Enforce hygiene, sanitation, and cleaning-in-place standards across the plant. Prepare the plant for internal, customer, and regulatory audits (e.g. Rwanda FDA, RSB) and close out findings. Ensure full product traceability from raw material intake to finished goods. 4. Cold Chain & Product Integrity Oversee chilling, freezing, and cold storage operations to keep product within required temperature ranges. Monitor and record temperatures across processing, storage, and loading points. Work with logistics to protect cold chain integrity through dispatch and distribution. 5. Shift Leadership & People Management Lead, schedule, and supervise shift supervisors, machine operators, and line workers. Train operators on safe equipment use, SOPs, hygiene, and food safety practices. Set clear performance expectations, give regular feedback, and contribute to performance reviews. Enforce occupational health and safety standards and lead incident investigations. 6. Production Reporting & KPIs Track and report daily, weekly, and monthly KPIs, including throughput, downtime, yield, and waste. Analyze performance trends and present root causes and action plans to management. Maintain accurate production, maintenance, and quality records. Support budgeting for plant operations, maintenance, and spare parts. Qualifications & Experience: Bachelor’s degree or advanced diploma in mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, industrial, or food process engineering, food science, or a related field. At least 5 years of experience in a processing plant (food, beverage, dairy, meat, poultry, or fish processing preferred), including hands-on supervision of machinery-heavy production lines. Strong process control skills and proven experience running preventive and corrective maintenance programs. Working knowledge of quality control and food safety standards such as HACCP, GMP, or ISO 22000. Cold chain or perishable-product experience is a strong plus. Proven ability to lead shift teams and operators in a production environment. Comfortable with production reporting and KPIs such as throughput, downtime, and yield; good working knowledge of Excel. Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose equipment and process issues quickly under pressure. Rwandan national, or already holding the right to work in Rwanda (Kivu Choice is not able to sponsor work permits for this role). Fluency in English and Kinyarwanda; French or Swahili is an advantage. B. Missions principales : Elaborer le registre des risques ; Identifier et évaluer les différents types de risques (financiers, opérationnels, de crédit, de marché, de liquidité, etc.) auxquels l'institution pourrait être exposée. Développer la cartographie des risques de l’institution Mettre en place des mécanismes de surveillance pour assurer un suivi continu des risques et ajuster les stratégies en fonction de l’évolution de l’environnement économique et réglementaire. Élaborer et proposer des mesures de mitigation des risques afin de réduire les risques à un niveau acceptable. Préparer et soumettre les rapports requis par les autorités de régulation, en s'assurant de leur exactitude et de leur conformité. Former les collaborateurs sur les pratiques de gestion des risques et de conformité. Développer des politiques et des procédures internes adaptées à la gestion des risques et à la conformité pour l'ensemble du personnel. Identifier, traiter et résoudre rapidement les situations de non-conformité ou les incidents de risques qui pourraient affecter l’intégrité et la réputation de la microfinance. Développer des plans d'action de gestion des risques et conformités. Fournir des rapports réguliers à la direction générale sur l'état de la gestion des risques et de la conformité au sein de l’institution. Communiquer et entretenir des relations avec les autorités réglementaires, en veillant à la transparence et à la bonne conduite de la microfinance. Mettre en œuvre et maintenir le programme de lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent et le financement du terrorisme. Implémenter un plan de continuité opérationnelle (business continuity plan) pour éviter qu’une interruption d’activité ne nuise à la société. C. Profil recherché : Une licence ou une maitrise en Gestion des Risques, Commerce, Management, Finance ou domaine connexe Minimum 4 ans d'expérience dans la gestion des risques et de la conformité idéalement en microfinance ou dans le secteur bancaire. Et doit être capable de parler couramment, écrire le français(obligatoire), l’Anglais et le Kinyarwanda. La maîtrise de différents outils technologiques ; La maîtrise des normes de sécurité financière, organisationnelle, écologique... Bonne connaissance des principes et pratiques de gestion des risques financiers Intégrité, rigueur, esprit d’analyse et de synthèse. Bonne aptitude managériale. Et avoir des Connaissances en Audit est un atout Les candidats intéressés par la présente offre et dont le profil répond aux critères mentionnés ci-Haut sont invités à envoyer : Une lettre de motivation, Une copie de la carte d’identité nationale, Un curriculum vitae (CV) détaillé, Des copies des diplômes universitaires et professionnels. Working closely with psychiatrists, nurses, psychologists, and other healthcare professionals, the GP will identify and manage medical risks, respond to adverse events, and ensure safe, coordinated patient care in accordance with approved clinical protocols, hospital policies, and applicable professional and regulatory standards. Key Responsibilities Conduct medical histories and physical examinations, review medications and comorbidities, identify contraindications and drug interactions, and request appropriate investigations or specialist assessments. Assess patients' medical status before treatment and communicate relevant findings and recommendations to the treating psychiatrist and multidisciplinary team. Monitor patients during treatment sessions in collaboration with the nursing team and respond to medical complications within professional competence. Recognize clinical deterioration, adverse reactions, and emergencies, initiate appropriate interventions, and activate hospital emergency pathways when necessary. Assess medical stability and discharge readiness, provide post-treatment precautions, and coordinate referrals and follow-up care. Participate in multidisciplinary case discussions and collaborate with the clinical team to ensure continuity and quality of care. Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential clinical records, including assessments, monitoring observations, interventions, and adverse events. Contribute to clinical audits, quality improvement, safety protocol reviews, and approved research activities in accordance with ethics approvals and confidentiality requirements. Comply with hospital policies, infection prevention standards, medication safety requirements, professional ethics, and continuing professional development requirements. Authority and Accountability The GP shall perform medical assessments, monitoring, interventions, and follow-up within the limits of professional registration, demonstrated competence, hospital privileges, and approved KTRC protocols. The GP's responsibilities include: Medical assessment and monitoring: Identifying medical risks, assessing patient stability, and supporting safe treatment delivery. Emergency management: Providing initial medical care, recognizing complications, and escalating cases requiring specialist intervention. Patient follow-up: Providing discharge advice, coordinating referrals, and supporting continuity of care. Documentation and quality improvement: Maintaining clinical records and contributing to audits, incident reporting, and approved research activities. Multidisciplinary collaboration: Communicating effectively with the treating psychiatrist and other healthcare professionals. Psychiatric diagnosis, psychiatric risk assessment, complex psychotropic medication decisions, and psychiatric treatment planning remain the responsibility of the treating psychiatrist. The GP shall not independently initiate or modify ketamine treatment outside approved protocols and the established authorization framework. Decisions regarding treatment eligibility, continuation, postponement, or discontinuation shall follow the designated clinical decision-making process. Qualifications and Experience Essential Bachelor's degree in Medicine or an equivalent recognized medical qualification. At least two (2) years of clinical experience as a medical practitioner. Valid registration and current practicing license from the relevant Rwandan medical regulatory authority. Demonstrated competence in medical assessment, clinical decision-making, and recognition of medical emergencies. Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification, or willingness to obtain it within the timeframe specified by the hospital. Strong communication, clinical documentation, and teamwork skills. Commitment to patient safety, confidentiality, professional ethics, and adherence to clinical protocols. Preferred Additional training in general practice, family medicine, internal medicine, or emergency medicine. Advanced Life Support (ALS) or equivalent emergency-care training. Experience in outpatient, day-care, or procedural services involving patient monitoring. Experience in mental health, substance use disorders, or psychiatric comorbidities. Training or experience in ketamine treatment or ketamine-assisted psychotherapy. Experience in clinical research, clinical audit, quality improvement, or electronic medical records. Required Technical and Clinical Skills Medical assessment and clinical decision-making. Identification of medical risks, contraindications, and drug interactions. Patient monitoring and initial management of medical emergencies. Medication safety and clinical documentation. Emergency response, referral, and escalation procedures. raw_text: Terms of Reference (TOR) – Operations & Logistics Manager Position: Operations & Logistics Manager Reports to: Academy Director Key Relationships: Academy Finance Manager, Educational Program Coordinator, Akagera National Park Management, appointed construction contractor and supervising architect Location: African Conservation Academy - Akagera National Park Contract: Fixed-term – 3 years. Start date: Estimated Mid-Late November 2026 Background The African Conservation Academy (hereafter referred to as the Academy) is a pioneering initiative that aims to address one of the most pressing challenges for conservation in Africa - the shortage of skilled, confident leaders to manage protected areas effectively. A purpose-built campus is to be developed for the Academy within Akagera National Park. Designed as a hands-on, applied training hub, the African Conservation Academy will deliver relevant, accessible training and development programmes for professionals from state, community, NGO, and privately managed protected areas from across the continent. Based in Akagera National Park, Rwanda, the Academy will immerse participants in the realities of conservation management - learning directly from a functioning yet evolving protected area. Position Purpose We are seeking an Operations and Logistics Manager who is committed to building Africa’s conservation talent. The role will ensure the smooth running of Academy operations and logistics by managing operational systems, resources, and personnel effectively in support of the Academy’s objectives. The role will also ensure a high degree of logistical and operational collaboration and alignment between the Academy and Akagera National Park. Additionally, during the construction of the campus, the Operations & Logistics Manager will oversee, with support of architectural supervision, the construction company contracted to carry out the build. Support the supervising engineer through any dispute arising under the construction contract, through final tests on completion of the construction, and manage the transition from construction into operation. Lead the planning, implementation, supervision and completion of infrastructure development and maintenance necessary post campus construction. LOGISTICS, STORES AND SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT Support the effective management, development, and operational readiness of the Academy and the day to day running of the facility, including but not limited to ensuring appropriate logistical support, equipment, and operational resources are available. Coordinate operations across the Academy and coordinate with Akagera Management Team to plan and implement those activities involving the park operations. Manage and supervise stores, procurement support functions, logistics operations and inventory systems, to ensure effective stock control procedures and uninterrupted availability of necessary supplies and equipment. Develop and manage systems that ensure accurate recording, accountability, transparency and efficiency in procurement and logistics processes. WORKSHOP, FLEET AND ASSET MANAGEMENT Supervise workshop operations, fleet management, maintenance personnel and vehicle drivers. Develop and implement maintenance schedules for vehicles and operational equipment, ensuring cost-effective practices are upheld. Maintain comprehensive maintenance records. Maintain accurate and up-to-date asset registers and management plans are in places for all vehicles, equipment, tools and operational assets. FACILITIES AND BUILDING MANAGEMENT Supervise facility operations and back of house personnel Develop and implement maintenance schedules for buildings, ensuring cost-effective practices are upheld. Maintain comprehensive maintenance records. Maintain accurate and up-to-date asset registers and management plans are in places for all infrastructure and associated assets. SYSTEMS IMPROVEMENT, COST MANAGEMENT AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY Develop and monitor operational budgets and ensure prudent utilization of resources. Identify and implement systems that improve operational efficiency, accountability and service delivery, without compromising operational effectiveness and safety. Establish performance monitoring systems for infrastructure, logistics and maintenance functions, Ensuring operational data, reports and records support informed decision-making. LANDSCAPE AND FIRE MANAGEMENT Work with Akagera Management Team to plan and implement a landscape restoration and ecological management plan for the Academy plot, integrating it into the park buffer zone. Lead the implementation of approved fire management plans and annual fire strategies for the Academy plot in partnership with Akagera Management Team, including fire prevention, preparedness, response and recovery activities. CONTRACTOR AND SERVICE PROVIDER MANAGEMENT Develop scopes of work, specifications and performance standards for contractors and service providers, with a focus on service delivery by local cooperatives where appropriate. Manage contractor performance to ensure compliance with contractual obligations, quality standards, safety requirements and project timelines, resolving any issues effectively. HEALTH, SAFETY AND RISK MANAGEMENT Promote and maintain a strong culture of occupational health and safety across all operational activities. Ensure compliance with the Academy’s policies, national legislation and industry safety standards. Conduct risk assessments and implement mitigation measures for all operations and logistics activities. Coordinate safety training, awareness programs and emergency preparedness initiatives. Ensure accidents, incidents and near misses are investigated, documented and corrective actions implemented. STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT AND COORDINATION Maintain effective working relationships with the Rwandan Development Board, local authorities, local communities, and other stakeholders in relation to operations and logistical activities for the Academy. Maintain close and effective relations with Akagera National Park in relation to operations and logistical activities for the Academy. REPORTING AND ADMINISTRATIVE RESPONSIBILITIES Prepare operations and logistics reports for submission to the Academy Director, as required. Monitor operational performance indicators and report on progress against agreed targets. Maintain accurate records, databases, plans, contracts, permits and operational documentation. Ensure compliance with the Academy’s policies, procedures, financial controls and reporting requirements. Perform any other duties assigned by the Academy Director that contribute to the effective management of the Academy. Equivalent practical experience will also be considered. A minimum of 10 years' progressively responsible experience, preferably in large-scale project or operations and logistics management. Sound financial management skills, including budgeting, cost control, resource planning, stock control, and procurement. Excellent organisational, reporting, communication and stakeholder engagement skills. Demonstrated experience in engaging with government agencies, local communities, and a range of service providers. Strong computer literacy and the ability to maintain accurate operational, maintenance and inventory records. A valid driving licence and fluency in English are essential. Proven experience working effectively in remote, rural, and multicultural environments. Willingness to relocate to Akagera National Park. Demonstrated ability to work effectively under pressure in a dynamic and challenging environment. Excellent decision-making and tactical judgement in complex, and changeable situations with tight deadlines. High levels of integrity, professionalism, self-discipline and resilience. raw_text: GAMICO Ltd Job Vacancy Announcement POSITION:PROCUREMENT OFFICER Company :GAMICO Ltd Location: Bashyamba Concession, Kigali Sector, Nyarugenge District, Rwanda Employment type: Full-time Reports to: Supply chain Section Leader Application deadline: 28th October 2026 About Us GAMICO Mining Company is one of the leading tin producers in Rwanda, operating at the Bashyamba concession in Kigali Sector, Nyarugenge District. With more than ten years of experience, we have built a strong reputation for quality production, safe operations, and responsible mining. We are committed to environmental stewardship and to the development of the communities in which we operate. As we continue to grow, we are looking for a detail-oriented and proactive Procurement Officer to join our team and help us source mining equipment, materials, and services efficiently, transparently, and at the best value. Key Responsibilities Purchase Requests and Planning Receive purchase requests from the stores and departments, and confirm that each one is properly completed and approved before any action is taken. Check the item description, specification, quantity and budget availability on every request. Plan purchases using stock levels and supplier lead times, and place orders in good time—ideally two weeks before consumable stock runs out—so nothing runs short. Combine similar requests where possible to obtain better prices and reduce the number of orders. Sourcing and Quotations Follow the procurement method set out in the company's Procurement Manual for every purchase, and obtain the quotations or bids that the method requires. Identify and maintain a list of reliable, approved suppliers for all goods, materials, equipment and services needed by the company. Compare the quotations or bids received on price, quality, delivery time and payment terms, and prepare the comparison for approval as required by the Procurement Manual. Negotiate prices and terms with suppliers in the best interest of the company, within the limits of the Procurement Manual. Confirm that the selected supplier is registered and can issue a valid EBM invoice. Purchase Orders Prepare and issue a PO to the selected supplier only after the purchase has been approved. State on every PO the item description, quantity, unit, agreed price, delivery date and delivery place. Record every PO in the Excel PO register, showing PO number, supplier, items, amount, order date, expected delivery date and status. Follow up with suppliers to make sure goods are delivered on the agreed date, and inform the requesting department and the store of any delay. Delivery, Invoices and Payment Support Work with the Store Keepers and the Equipment Store Officer to make sure every delivery is physically counted and matched against the PO, the supplier delivery note and the EBM invoice, and that the price agrees before the invoice is passed for payment. Resolve shortages, damaged goods, wrong items and price differences with suppliers, and arrange returns, replacements or credit notes. Hand over the complete set of documents (PO, delivery note and EBM invoice) to the Equipment Store Officer for receiving in QBO, and to Finance for payment. Supplier Management Evaluate supplier performance regularly on quality, delivery time, price and service. Handle any claim about the quality of goods supplied directly with the supplier, supported by the Store Keeper's and the user department's records. Keep supplier contracts, agreements and contact details up to date and filed. Report poor or unreliable suppliers to the Procurement Section Leader, with a recommendation on whether to continue buying from them. Records and Reporting Keep all procurement documents (requests, quotations, comparisons, POs, delivery notes, EBM invoices) filed in order and available for audit. Prepare a weekly and monthly procurement report showing purchases made, pending orders, late deliveries and cost savings. Ethics and General Responsibilities Act with honesty and integrity, and avoid any conflict of interest in dealing with suppliers. Do not accept gifts, favours or payments from suppliers or potential suppliers. Follow company procurement policies and procedures, and the applicable laws and tax requirements. Perform any other related duties assigned by the Procurement Section Leader. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Economics or a related field [2-3] years of relevant procurement experience, preferably in mining, construction, or another heavy industry Professional certification (e.g., CIPS) is an added advantage Solid knowledge of procurement procedures, contract management, and tendering processes Familiarity with mining equipment and supply chains is an added advantage Strong negotiation, analytical, and communication skills What We Offer Competitive salary commensurate with experience Health insurance Opportunities for professional development and career growth A safe, collaborative, and supportive work environment How to Apply Send your CV and a cover letter to info@gamico.rw with the subject line "Procurement Officer Application" by 28th October 2026. title: Investment Lead
raw_text: About Inzira Creative Partners Inzira Creative Partners is the sector infrastructure for Rwanda’s creative economy, coordinating the Creative Rwanda consortium and connecting creatives and creative enterprises to markets, catalytic finance and policy. The Creative Rwanda Program is delivered through a partnership with the Mastercard Foundation and is led and coordinated by Inzira Creative Partners, in collaboration with Gahaya Links and MASS Design Group. Within the program, Inzira leads ecosystem coordination and financial inclusion. Nibigira, from the Kinyarwanda for “it guides us”, is our catalytic fund for young creative entrepreneurs. It offers finance designed around how creative work actually earns. There is no land collateral, repayment follows income rather than the calendar, and every investment comes with business support built in.About the role Most Rwandan creatives have never been offered finance that fits how they earn. We are building a fund that does, and we’re looking for an Investment Lead to build and run it day to day. This is a builder’s role. The fund is in its first cohorts. You will shape how it works in practice, from finding creatives who have never been considered bankable to seeing capital come back so it can go out again.What you’ll drivePipeline and origination Build a pipeline of creative entrepreneurs across Rwanda, including outside Kigali. Make sure the application process is open to everyone the fund is for. That means bilingual Kinyarwanda and English, accessible formats, and support for applicants who can’t produce a written plan. Assessment and investment decisions Assess creatives on their practice, the demand for their work and their potential, not only on credit history or collateral. Prepare investment papers and bring sector insight on creative business models, seasonality and risk. Make sure every investment is documented, with a clear rationale, repayment plan and follow-up. Portfolio and repayment Monitor the portfolio so repayment follows what creatives actually earn. Spot repayment barriers early and act on them, so capital returns and can be invested again. Inclusion and support Make sure the fund reaches young women, rural creatives, refugees and persons with disabilities, and track it in disaggregated data at every stage. Make sure every investment comes with support, from financial literacy, pricing and business planning to mentorship and market connections. Partnerships and growth Lead conversations with banks, microfinance institutions and fintechs to build a pathway from Nibigira into mainstream credit. Pilot finance for emerging creative sub-sectors and turn what the fund learns into the case for its growth. Who you are At least five years in investment, credit or portfolio management, ideally in inclusive finance, impact investing or SME lending in Rwanda or a comparable market. Working knowledge of blended finance, including grants, returnable grants and revenue-based or shared-risk structures, and comfort working within shared governance. Experience reading irregular cash flows and assessing businesses that traditional lenders turn away. Able to turn portfolio data into pipeline and product decisions. A degree in finance, economics, business or a related field. A master’s or investment qualification is an advantage. Fluent in Kinyarwanda and English. Familiarity with Rwanda’s creative industries is welcome but not required. The ability to learn a new sector’s business models quickly, and to respect them, is. How you work You see a creative’s portfolio, contracts and audience as evidence, and you know the difference between a risky business and an excluded one. You’re as comfortable at a cooperative meeting in the provinces as in an investment committee, and credible in both. You’re disciplined about documentation, because a fund’s credibility depends on it. You hold inclusion as both commitment and design principle. Women, rural and refugee young creatives, and persons with disabilities within the creative sector, are part of Rwanda’s future. What we offer Opportunity to help lead a vibrant, purpose-driven organisation that fosters creativity and community engagement. A collaborative, dynamic environment committed to creative and cultural impact. The chance to shape the future of creative finance and the creative economy in Rwanda, Africa and beyond. Details Full-time, two-year fixed term with a six-month probation, renewable. Based in Kigali, with regular travel across Rwanda. Reports to the Executive Director. title: Regional Human Rights Specialist
raw_text: Regional Human Rights Specialist, Africa Rwanda Full-Time GLOBAL CONSERVATION Job Description Reports To: Director, Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) Location: Kigali, Rwanda (or another WCS Africa hub location) Country Program/Sector: APAMU /Africa Program Position Type: Full-time Scope/Capacity: Africa-wide Coordinates with: APAMU Team, Rights & Communities, Rights & Communities Regional and National Staff, Regional Leadership Teams, Country Directors, Landscape Leads, Protected Area Managers, Law Enforcement Advisors, Program Development Teams, and Technical Working Groups About Us The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a private, nonprofit U.S. organization founded in 1895. Its mission is to preserve wildlife and wild places by understanding critical issues, developing science-based solutions, and taking conservation action that benefits nature and humanity. With more than a century of experience, long-term commitments in dozens of landscapes, a presence in more than 60 countries, and experience creating more than 150 protected areas worldwide, WCS has accumulated the biological knowledge, cultural understanding, and partnerships necessary to ensure that wildlife and wild places thrive alongside local communities. WCS recognizes that nature and people are intrinsically linked, and that biological and cultural diversity are interdependent, mutually reinforcing and often co-evolved. Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities frequently represent the most active defenders of nature, and we believe that respecting and protecting the rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities reflects our global commitment to equity and justice and is our best pathway to achieving durable conservation. About the Africa Program WCS manages one of the largest conservation portfolios in Africa, supporting protected and conserved areas, community-led conservation, key biodiversity landscapes, species conservation initiatives, and wildlife law enforcement efforts across multiple countries. Globally, WCS also supports Indigenous and Traditional Territories, a growing opportunity to center guardians of nature and to secure their rights. The Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) seeks to ensure that conservation outcomes are achieved in a manner that applies WCS policies, principles and commitments. The Global Rights and Communities (R&C) unit provides guidance and tools across WCS countries to promote community conservation, ensure social safeguards and promote respect for human rights and positive relationships with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and other rights holders. This position will play an important role in coordinating and contributing to a standardized approach to human rights protection in Africa, with the guidance of APAMU, Global R&C and close collaboration with regional and country teams. Job Purpose The Regional Human Rights Specialist will lead and support the standardization of human rights integration and rights-based approaches across WCS conservation programs throughout Africa. The position will provide strategic and technical guidance to country programs and field sites to support human rights integration in conservation law enforcement, conduct human rights impact analyses, assist in investigation or fact-finding around human rights issues as requested, develop recommendations for country programs or landscapes to address human rights issues and risks, and oversee the review of rights-respecting Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for field operations. This position reports to the Director of Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU), and will play a critical role in the APAMU team in fulfilling the needs of a human rights based approach. The position will maintain a dotted line of reporting to the Senior Human Rights Specialist in Rights & Communities Global, for final approval and review of substantive human rights products and in order to coordinate with broader WCS policy and approaches outside of Africa. The position will also coordinate closely with regional and country level human rights, law enforcement, safeguards and communities staff. This position will require significant travel to remote field locations and sites where WCS works, and working with diverse teams from different country programs. The candidate will be expected to undertake planning and coordination as necessary with global, regional and country or site-level counterparts. Major Responsibilities 1. Human Rights Strategy and Integration Work with Senior Human Rights Specialist to ensure the implementation of WCS's rights-based conservation approach across all Africa programs. Coordinate with Regional Social Safeguards leads to support country programs and landscapes to integrate human rights into conservation planning, project design, budgets, monitoring, and reporting. Provide technical guidance on international human rights standards applicable to conservation programming. Promote alignment between WCS sites, country and regional level management, APAMU, and Rights & Communities. Support the development and review of organizational guidance, tools, frameworks, and operational procedures related to human rights. 2. Human Rights Impact Analysis and Risk Management Conduct human rights impact assessments and analyses for new sites and other situations as needed. Identify actual and potential human rights risks associated with conservation interventions and recommend practical mitigation and management measures. Contribute to the development and maintenance of systems for tracking human rights risks, corrective actions, lessons learned, and emerging trends across Africa programs. 3. Human Rights and Conservation Law Enforcement Work closely with the APAMU Law Enforcement Strategist and Senior Human Rights Specialist to provide strategic guidance on the integration of human rights principles into conservation law enforcement operations. Support law enforcement teams, site managers, and country programs to ensure that internationally recognized human rights standards are observed, and protocols are adequate for monitoring, and training. Support the development, review, and implementation of rights-respecting law enforcement policies, protocols, and operational guidance. 4. Development of Rights-Respecting SOPs Review Africa-level Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that embed human rights principles into field operations as needed together with regional safeguards leads, based on WCS institutional policies. 5. Training and capacity building Design and deliver human rights trainings with a focus on practical application of human rights protection and human rights-based approaches in the context of field implementation, community conservation and conservation law enforcement (or equivalent) 6. Other tasks as needed Review protocols and process relating to mainstreaming of gender equity, respect for the rights of Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and underrepresented groups in program design and management. Contribute technical content for donor reports and organizational reporting related to human rights commitments and achievements. Qualification Requirements Advanced degree in Law or other relevant field with a specialization in human rights; a first degree with relevant experience and certificates can be accepted in lieu of an advanced degree. Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in human rights advocacy, research, policy or monitoring and reporting. Proven experience working directly with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, civil society organizations, and/or government stakeholders in the context of Africa. Fluency in English and ability to work professionally in French. Desirable Qualifications Experience in conservation programs or issues relating to conservation. Experience with grassroots advocacy or human rights defenders. Fluency in Portuguese or African languages relevant to program areas. Core Competencies and Skills Technical Competencies Strong knowledge of international human rights standards and frameworks, and regional African frameworks Knowledge of both civil law and common law based systems for law enforcement. Understanding of human rights-based approaches to conservation and development including institutional due diligence practices. Demonstrated experience conducting human rights assessments and risk assessments and to develop appropriate methodologies. Understanding of gender integration, Indigenous Peoples rights. Experience developing policies, guidance documents, and operational procedures. Professional Skills Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills. Effective at organization, time-management, and self-directed field work. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Strong stakeholder engagement and interview skills. Ability to work effectively across cultures and multidisciplinary teams. Ability to influence and support change across diverse country programs. raw_text: AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET Entreprise Palast Tours & Travels, Kigali, Rwanda Poste Guide Conférencier (Francophone) Type de Contrat Contrat-Cadre (Framework Contract) Type de prestations Prestations à temps partiel pendant la durée d’un circuit de voyage de groupe au Rwanda [dates à confirmer]et suivant la disponibilité du Guide Conférencier Nombre de postes à pourvoir Cinq (5) Supérieur hiérarchique Responsable des Opérations / General Manager Lieu de travail Kigali et différentes destinations touristiques à travers le Rwanda 1. Présentation du poste Palast Tours & Travels, affiliée à Palast Group Ltd, est une Entreprise qui offre des services touristiques en Afrique de l’Est en général et au Rwanda en particulier comme Agence Receptive(Destination Management Company, DMC). Elle est spécialisée dans des expériences de voyage de luxe sur mesure. En partenariat avec un tour-opérateur francophone spécialisé dans les voyages culturels à travers le monde, Palast Tours & Travels propose des circuits, des séjours thématiques et des voyages sur mesure, accompagnés par des guides-conférenciers experts en histoire, art et patrimoine. Ses voyages s’adressent aux voyageurs en quête de découvertes culturelles approfondies, souvent en petits groupes. Palast Tours & Travels recherche 5 Guides-Conférenciers francophones d’exception pour accompagner des groupes de voyageurs internationaux francophones tout au long de leur séjour au Rwanda. Contrairement à un guide touristique classique, le Guide-Conférencier est le compagnon culturel et intellectuel du groupe. Il/elle anime des présentations approfondies, structurées et captivantes, et répond aux questions des visiteurs sur l’histoire, la société, l’économie, la géographie et les traditions du Rwanda, afin que les voyageurs repartent avec une compréhension approfondie du pays, au-delà des seuls souvenirs de ses paysages. 2. Principales responsabilités Conférences et interprétation Organiser et animer de courtes conférences/Exposés dans les hôtels, pendant les soirées, sur des sujets d’intérêt culturel, historique et autres qui intéressent les voyageurs, après leurs visites et activités touristiques. Présenter des exposés et commentaires captivants pendant les transferts, lors des visites de sites, ainsi que lors des visites de mémoriaux et de sites culturels. Expliquer l’histoire du Rwanda, depuis les royaumes précoloniaux et la période coloniale jusqu’à l’indépendance, au Génocide perpétré contre les Tutsis en 1994, à la réconciliation et à la reconstruction nationale, avec exactitude, sensibilité et respect. Présenter les réalités actuelles du Rwanda : économie et vision de développement, gouvernance, géopolitique régionale, système éducatif, système de santé, vie communautaire et conservation de la nature. Faire découvrir la culture et les traditions locales, notamment la langue, la musique et la danse, l’artisanat, la gastronomie, ainsi que les différentes initiatives de de développement communautaires et social comme l’Umuganda et les Imihigo et autres. Interaction avec les voyageurs Répondre avec assurance et de manière approfondie aux questions du groupe et encourager les échanges et les discussions. Adapter le contenu et le ton aux centres d’intérêt, à l’âge et au rythme du groupe. Aborder les sujets sensibles avec professionnalisme, neutralité et empathie. Accompagnement et soutien au bon déroulement du circuit Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le chauffeur-guide et l’équipe opérationnelle de Palast afin de respecter le programme et les horaires prévus. Informer chaque jour les voyageurs du programme, leur donner le contexte des sites visités et leur expliquer les règles de savoir-vivre et les usages culturels à respecter. Coordonner, lorsque nécessaire, avec le personnel des sites, les guides de musées et les représentants des communautés locales. Signaler immédiatement à l’équipe opérationnelle toute préoccupation ou tout incident concernant les voyageurs. Compte rendu Fournir, à la fin du circuit, un retour d’expérience sur le séjour du groupe et formuler des recommandations visant à améliorer le programme. 3. Qualifications requises Diplôme universitaire, de préférence en Histoire, idéalement de niveau Master (Maîtrise), Les diplômes dans des domaines connexes tels que les Sciences politiques, l’Anthropologie, la Géographie, la Communication ou les Sciences sociales peuvent être pris en considération s’ils sont accompagnés d’une solide connaissance historique. Connaissances requises Excellente connaissance, approfondie et équilibrée, du Rwanda dans toutes ses dimensions : Géographie, Économie, Vie sociale et système éducatif, Histoire et géopolitique, Culture et traditions locales Capacité à répondre avec aisance, précision et crédibilité aux questions susceptibles d’être posées par les voyageurs. Compétences linguistiques Excellente maîtrise du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, de niveau natif ou quasi natif. Une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais et du kinyarwanda constitue un atout. Compétences en communication Excellentes aptitudes à la prise de parole en public et aisance devant un groupe. Capacité à raconter et à transmettre des informations de manière claire, captivante et structurée, afin de retenir l’attention d’un public international et instruit. 4. Qualités et compétences souhaitées Expérience préalable en tant que guide, conférencier, enseignant ou interprète culturel, de préférence auprès de visiteurs internationaux. Professionnalisme, ponctualité, présentation soignée et respect des sensibilités culturelles et religieuses. Personnalité chaleureuse, patience et excellentes qualités relationnelles. Flexibilité pour travailler de longues journées et voyager à travers le pays. Bonne connaissance des parcs nationaux du Rwanda, des sites mémoriels, des musées et des sites du patrimoine est souhaitée. 5. Dossier de candidature Les candidats intéressés devront soumettre : Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt adressée au General Manager de Palast Tours & Travels Un Curriculum Vitae mis à jour ; Une copie de leur(s) diplôme(s) ; Les coordonnées d’au moins deux références professionnelles ; Une courte vidéo ou un enregistrement audio de présentation (facultatif mais vivement recommandé), permettant d’apprécier leur expression et leur aisance en français. Les candidatures doivent être envoyées à l’adresse mail suivante : recruitment@palastgroup.rw Date limite de candidature : 30 Octobre 2026 Processus de sélection Examen des CV et vérification des qualifications ; Entretien en français portant notamment sur la connaissance du Rwanda ; 3.
