title: Civil & Structural Technician
experience_raw: Entry level (1 to 3 years of experience)
raw_text: Description Job Title: Civil & Structural Technician Department: Infrastructure Duty Station: UGHE, Butaro, Rwanda Reports To: Civil and Structure Engineering Manager Employment Type: Full-time 1. JOB PURPOSE The Civil & Structural Technician will provide practical technical and maintenance support for the University's civil infrastructure, buildings, and external facilities. The position will be responsible for routine inspection, preventive maintenance, minor civil repairs, building-fabric works, site measurements, workmanship checks, defect reporting, and support to approved facilities improvement projects. The successful candidate should be a hands-on, multi-skilled technician capable of working independently on routine tasks while also supporting contractors, artisans, engineers and facilities staff. The position requires good practical knowledge of civil works, basic structural elements, building maintenance, drainage, paving, and general building fabric repairs. The technician will be expected to identify defects and unsafe conditions, carry out authorized remedial works, maintain accurate work records, and promptly escalate major structural, safety or specialist issues to the responsible supervisor. 2. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES A. Civil Infrastructure Inspection and Maintenance Inspect assigned external civil infrastructure and building elements on a routine basis. Inspect and maintain paths, paving, steps, surface drains, gullies, and minor boundary works. Identify and report on settlement, cracking, blocked drainage, trip hazards, erosion and other defects. Identify potential concerns affecting retaining structures or other structural elements and escalate them appropriately. Carry out authorized minor repairs and maintenance works. Clear authorized drainage blockages and maintain serviceable access routes. Coordinate with gardening and other maintenance staff where vegetation affects drainage, access or civil infrastructure. Maintain accurate inspection and maintenance records. B. Building Fabric and Minor Civil Works Execute approved minor civil and building fabric maintenance works. Undertake practical repairs involving finishes, doors, roofs, drainage and other related building elements where safe and within assigned competence. Prepare work areas, tools, equipment, and materials before commencing assigned tasks. Take measurements and quantities required for maintenance and repair work. Carry out minor masonry, plastering, concrete, paving, drainage and related repair activities. Inspect completed works for workmanship and identify defects requiring correction. Complete assigned snagging and remedial work. Maintain clean, safe, and organized work areas. C. Facilities Improvement and Project Support Support approved civil components of facilities improvement projects. Assist with site measurements, setting out, access arrangements and preparation of materials. Provide practical site support to engineers, project managers, and contractors. Monitor assigned works and provide observations on workmanship, materials, and defects. Assist with snag identification and closure. Support civil interfaces associated with projects such as drainage, water infrastructure, tanks, STP works, grey-water systems, fire-protection infrastructure and other facilities improvements as assigned. Maintain records of site observations, measurements, completed works, and outstanding items. Work within approved drawings, specifications, scope, and instructions. D. Contractor and Workmanship Support Support the Facilities/Infrastructure team in monitoring contractor activities within assigned areas. Verify dimensions, quantities and completed works where assigned. Observe workmanship and report defects or deviations from approved requirements. Assist in preparing areas for contractor activities and coordinating access. Participate in inspections and snagging exercises. Provide evidence of completed works and support project close-out documentation. Escalate major technical, structural or specialist works to the responsible engineer/manager. E. Tools, Materials and Work Planning Prepare required tools, equipment, and materials for assigned work. Ensure appropriate tools are used safely and correctly. Report shortages, damaged equipment, or unsuitable materials. Assist with material measurements and usage records. Maintain tools and equipment in good working conditions. Keep work areas clean and properly protected during maintenance activities. F. Health, Safety, Quality and Environmental Compliance Comply with all applicable workplace health and safety requirements. Conduct pre-work checks and identify hazards before commencing activities. Use appropriate PPE and safe working methods. Follow safe procedures for working at height, manual handling, dust-producing activities, access works and use of tools/equipment. Protect building users, staff, visitors and property while carrying out maintenance work. Maintain good housekeeping at all work locations. Promptly report hazards, incidents, near misses and unsafe conditions. Stop and escalate work where conditions exceed the technician's competence or authorization. Maintain required quality and maintenance documentation. G. Documentation and Reporting Maintain complete work orders and maintenance records. Record inspections, defects, measurements, materials used and completed works. Provide photographic or other evidence of completed works where required. Record and follow up on outstanding defects and snags. Provide regular updates to the supervisor responsible. Ensure assigned work orders are properly closed out. Maintain accurate records of safety observations, incidents, and near misses. 3. KEY DELIVERABLES The Civil & Structural Technician will be expected to deliver: Safe and serviceable external civil infrastructure. Timely completion of assigned minor civil and building maintenance works. Accurate inspection and defect records. Properly completed and documented work orders. Effective identification and escalation of structural and major civil defects. Quality workmanship on authorized in-house repairs. Effective support to contractors and facilities improvement projects. Timely closure of assigned snags and defects. Proper material and tool utilization. Compliance with health, safety, and quality requirements. 4. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE Minimum Qualifications Advanced Diploma in Civil Engineering, Civil Engineering Technology, Building Technology, Construction Technology or related technical field. A recognized technical/vocational qualification in civil construction or building works may also be considered supported by relevant practical experience. Experience • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant practical experience in civil works, building maintenance, construction or facilities maintenance. • Practical experience in the maintenance of buildings and external infrastructure is highly desirable. • Experience working with contractors and multidisciplinary maintenance teams is an advantage. • Experience in an institutional, commercial, healthcare, educational, or similar environment is desirable. 5. TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES The candidate should demonstrate practical competence in: General civil construction and maintenance. Concrete and minor reinforced concrete works. Masonry and plastering. Paving and external work. Surface drainage and gullies. Minor building repairs and building fabric maintenance. Basic understanding of structural elements and common structural defects. Basic site measurement and quantity take-off. Reading and interpreting basic construction drawings. Basic setting out and levels. Identification and reporting of construction defects. Basic use and care for construction tools and equipment. Workmanship inspection and snagging. Basic maintenance documentation and reporting. Occupational health and safety procedures. 6. HANDS-ON / MULTI-SKILLED REQUIREMENT The successful candidate should be willing and able to perform practical hands-on duties rather than functioning solely in an office or supervisory capacity. The technician should be capable of assisting with or performing, within their competence and authorization: Minor masonry repairs. Concrete repairs. Plastering and patching. Paving repairs. Drainage cleaning and minor repairs. Kerb and walkway repairs. Minor boundary wall repairs. Door and building fabric repairs. Minor roof-related maintenance support. Painting and surface preparation. Basic carpentry-related building maintenance. General facilities repair and maintenance activities. Preparation of work areas and materials. Site housekeeping and protection. Where a task requires specialist engineering design, structural assessment, major construction, electrical/mechanical expertise or other specialist competence, the technician must escalate the matter to the responsible professional or contractor. 7. BEHAVIOURAL AND PERSONAL COMPETENCIES The successful candidate should demonstrate: Strong practical and hands-on attitude. Reliability and punctuality. Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Good attention to detail. Strong safety awareness. Good problem-solving ability. Ability to identify and report defects accurately. Good communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to follow instructions, drawings, and technical requirements. Good work discipline and housekeeping. Ability to prioritize maintenance tasks. Professional conduct when working around staff, students, patients, visitors, and contractors. Willingness to learn and undertake different facilities-related tasks within the technician's competence. 8. REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS The Civil & Structural Technician will report to the Civil and Structure Engineering Manager and will work closely with: Civil/Structural Engineers. Facilities and maintenance personnel. MEP technicians. Project managers. Contractors and artisans. Procurement and stores personnel. Security and other relevant institutional departments. 9. AUTHORITY AND LIMITS OF RESPONSIBILITY The technician is authorized to undertake approved routine maintenance and minor civil works within their demonstrated competence. The technician shall not independently approve, design or execute major structural works or specialist works outside their competence. Structural defects, major cracks, significant settlement, major drainage failures, structural instability, major alterations and other high-risk or specialist works shall be promptly reported and escalated to the responsible engineer/manager. Major works and specialist contractor activities remain subject to the University's approved project management, engineering and procurement processes. 10. PERFORMANCE INDICATORS Performance will be assessed against: Completion of assigned maintenance work orders within agreed timelines. Quality and durability of completed repairs. Accuracy and completeness of inspection and maintenance records. Timely identification and escalation of defects and safety risks. Effective closure of assigned snags. Compliance with approved drawings, instructions, and work methods. Compliance with health and safety requirements. Proper use of tools, materials, and equipment. Effective support for projects and contractors. Good housekeeping and protection of institutional facilities. How to Apply Applicants should provide: (1) curriculum vitae, (2) degree, (3) a cover letter describing your interest in UGHE and relevant experience. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page. University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Organizational Profile UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. Through an academic experience uniquely rooted in the values of equity, students are empowered to both ease suffering at the bedside and drive transformational, systemic changes to the health system. UGHE is an initiative of Partners In Health (PIH), an internationally recognized non-profit organization whose mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. In over nearly three decades of operating alongside public sectors in countries around the world, PIH has developed a model to deliver high quality healthcare to some of the world’s most marginalized communities. Nowhere has this impact been more profound than in Rwanda, where Inshuti Mu Buzima—PIH’s sister organization—and our government partners have driven innovation for a decade. Members of the UGHE community are tenacious and resolute in our drive to attain social justice, make common cause with those in need, listen to and learn from others, and operate with honesty and humility as we uphold academic integrity and intellectual curiosity. The University of Global Health Equity seeks individuals committed to these values to join the team. Commitment to Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Sexual Harassment At UGHE, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work—including community members—as well as our students, contractors, staff, and visitors to our campus are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and any form of systemic abuse, whilst reducing risk and vulnerabilities. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with UGHE’s policy. UGHE will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of fraud, harassment, sexual harassment and any form of systemic abuse or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By applying, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures. Apply

title: Zero Out Of School Children Project Director
raw_text: ROLE PURPOSE The Government of Rwanda, through the Ministry of Education (MINEDUC), has signed a framework agreement with Educate A Child (EAC) to achieve zero out-of-school children (OOSC) at primary level. MINEDUC selected Save the Children as implementing partner, working in consortium with Humanity & Inclusion (HI) and NUDOR. The goal is improved access to, and retention in, equitable primary education for all Rwandan children. The five-year project (2023–2028) aims to enrol and retain 177,119 children at primary level by: (1) strengthening identification, enrolment, attendance and retention of OOSC at school level; (2) empowering communities and families to support enrolment and retention; and (3) strengthening policies, data and feedback systems on OOSC. The Project Director holds overall accountability for technical leadership, strategic and operational management, consortium coordination and donor compliance of the ZOOSC Project. In line with the Save the Children Operating Model (consortium/Chief of Party-type awards), the post-holder is the lead representative of the consortium, the primary link with EAC, MINEDUC and partners, and ensures quality, timeliness and value for money of all results, reports and financial management. The Project Director works closely with the Country Office SMT, the DPO (budget holder) and Save the Children US (Member) to ensure the award is delivered in compliance with donor and SCI requirements. raw_text: Communications Intern (Kigali, Rwanda) – VIA Foundation Location: Kigali, Rwanda Contract Type: Internship (6 months, paid) Start Date: November 1, 2026 Work Authorization: This position requires regular in-person work from VIA Foundation’s office in Kigali, Rwanda, alongside staff at VIA Foundation and its core partner WRI Africa. Existing work authorization in Rwanda is required. VIA Foundation cannot sponsor a work visa. About Vumbuzi Impact Africa (VIA) Foundation VIA Foundation is a recently founded financial intermediary organization dedicated to supporting the acceleration and scale-up of ecosystem restoration efforts across member countries of the African Forest Landscape Restoration Initiative (AFR100). The mission of VIA Foundation is to provide innovative financial solutions and strategic support to restoration champions, the local organizations that mobilize communities to restore degraded land. As a trusted and up-and-coming intermediary, VIA Foundation intends to mobilize resources, foster partnerships, and drive the implementation of sustainable landscape restoration projects. Its goal is to enhance ecosystem resilience, empower local communities, and contribute to global climate goals. With its growing team and partnerships with leading institutions, VIA Foundation aims to create a legacy of restored landscapes that thrive both ecologically and economically, ensuring a sustainable future for generations to come. VIA Foundation is a partner of TerraFund, a financing consortium that currently funds, trains, and monitors 200+ restoration projects across Africa. TerraFund focuses on deploying grants, low-interest loans, and equity finance to organizations in three key landscapes: the Lake Kivu & Rusizi River Basin (in Burundi, DRC, and Rwanda), the Greater Rift Valley of Kenya, and the Ghana Cocoa Belt. These portfolios are managed through the World Resources Institute’s TerraMatch platform, an end-to-end system that hosts open calls for proposals, connects champions with technical assistance, and tracks the progress of funded projects through a standard monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) protocol. With this data, VIA Foundation is building new partnerships that catalyze finance for restoration outcomes. Internship Highlight: VIA Foundation seeks a Communications Intern to help tell the story of locally led restoration across Africa. Working from the Kigali office, you will help build the foundation’s young public voice producing content for its website and LinkedIn, capturing stories from the restoration champions it finances, and assembling the communications materials that support its partnerships and fundraising. This is a hands-on learning role designed for a recent university graduate who writes well, is curious about restoration and climate finance, and wants to build a professional portfolio. You will be expected to draft, design, publish materials, and take ownership of the pieces assigned to you. You will report to the Grants & Finance Specialist and work closely with VIA Foundation’s Project Managers, its Field Coordinators in Rwanda, Kenya, and Ghana, and communications colleagues at VIA Foundation’s technical partner WRI Africa. Over six months, you will see how an emerging pan-African institution positions itself with funders, governments, and the communities restoring degraded land. Key Responsibilities: Content Creation (50%) Draft and edit short-form content champion profiles, field stories, blog posts, newsletter copy, event recaps, and captions in clear, accessible English. Work with Project Managers and Field Coordinators to gather photographs, quotes, and stories from restoration sites and nurseries through both the TerraMatch platform and turn them into publishable material. Build simple visual assets — social graphics, slide templates, one-pagers, and carousels — using Canva or similar tools, in line with VIA Foundation’s brand guidelines. Maintain an organized library of photos, videos, logos, consent forms, and approved messaging so that materials can be reused quickly and correctly. Support the drafting of communications products that strengthen fundraising and donor engagement, such as impact snapshots, portfolio highlights, and annual report sections. Support the preparation of materials for external forums where VIA Foundation is represented. Digital Channel Management (50%) Maintain and update content on via-foundation.org, including news items, partner pages, and vacancy postings. Prepare, schedule, and publish posts across VIA Foundation’s LinkedIn and monitor comments and messages for follow-up. Build a mailing list of VIA Foundation’s partners through which to share news and updates. Maintain the communications calendar, tracking upcoming publications, events, campaign moments, and portfolio milestones. Compile monthly analytics on website traffic and social media performance, and flag what is working and what is not. What you will learn: How a financial intermediary communicates restoration finance to funders, governments, and local organizations. Practical digital communications skills: content management systems, social publishing and analytics tools, and basic design and multimedia editing. How to mine online reporting systems to tell stories from the field. A portfolio of published work — written pieces, visual assets, and campaign materials — that you can carry into your next role. What you will need: Education: A completed bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, international development, environmental studies, or a related field. Recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Experience: Up to 2 years of experience — including internships, student media, volunteer work, or freelance assignments — in communications, content creation, or digital media. Excellent written English, with a demonstrated ability to turn complex or technical material into clear, engaging copy. A portfolio, writing samples, or links to published work are required. Familiarity with major social media platforms and how organizations use them, including basic content planning and audience engagement. Working knowledge of design and editing tools such as Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or CapCut; comfort with photography or short-form video is an advantage. Basic experience with website content management, e.g., Drupal, and with social media or web analytics is an advantage. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage several assignments against deadlines in a small, fast-moving team. Demonstrated interest in ecosystem restoration, climate, agriculture, or sustainable development. Comfort receiving and acting on editorial feedback across multiple rounds of revision. Languages: You will be proficient in written and spoken English and fluent in Kinyarwanda. Additional fluency in French and/or Swahili is an asset. Requirements: You must have an existing right to work in Rwanda and be able to work in person from VIA Foundation’s Kigali office. Travel: Willingness to travel occasionally to restoration sites in Rwanda to gather stories and content. Internship Terms: This is a full-time, six-month paid internship based in Kigali, Rwanda. The intern will receive a monthly stipend in RWF. The intern will receive regular supervision, feedback, and mentoring, and will have access to learning opportunities across VIA Foundation and its partner network. How to apply? A 1-page cover letter specifying why you are an excellent fit for the internship. Two short writing samples, or links to a portfolio of communications work (published articles, social campaigns, videos, or design pieces). Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Applications are due by 23:59 CAT on October 10, 2026. Late applications will not be considered. Note on Equal Opportunity VIA Foundation is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that reflects the communities it serves. Key Responsibilities 3.1 Strategic MEL Leadership and Performance Management – Weight 30% Lead the development, implementation and continuous improvement of FAWE Rwanda’s integrated MEL system, ensuring alignment with the Strategic Plan, annual plans, project frameworks, donor requirements and FAWE regional frameworks. Facilitate periodic performance reviews and provide strategic advice to management and programme teams on corrective actions, programme effectiveness and evidence-informed decision-making. Strengthen integration of results-based management and MEL throughout the programme cycle, ensuring measurement extends beyond activities and reach to outcomes, quality, sustainability and contribution to change. 3.2 Data, Research, Evaluation and Evidence Generation- Weight 20% Establish and maintain robust systems for collecting, managing, analysing and safeguarding high-quality quantitative and qualitative programme and institutional data. Lead baselines, assessments, surveys, tracer studies, evaluations and other strategic research, ensuring methodological quality and credibility of findings. Strong experience in designing, conducting or managing quantitative and qualitative research, surveys, assessments and evaluations, including quality assurance of externally commissioned studies, with demonstrated ability to analyse and translate findings into actionable recommendations. Strong analytical and digital capabilities, including proficiency in relevant tools such as Excel, Power BI/Tableau, SPSS, and KoboToolbox/ODK or comparable platforms, with experience in data visualization, dashboards and knowledge management considered an advantage. Demonstrated ability to facilitate organizational learning and adaptive management, including translating performance evidence, research findings and lessons into strategic and operational improvements. Excellent strategic thinking, analytical, problem-solving, communication and report-writing skills, with the ability to communicate complex evidence clearly to technical and non-technical audiences and constructively influence management, programme teams and partners. Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, with demonstrated ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams and engage government, development partners, research institutions, implementing partners and other stakeholders. Demonstrated commitment to professional integrity, research ethics, data confidentiality, gender equality, inclusion and safeguarding, with the ability to apply gender-responsive and inclusive approaches throughout MEL processes. 5. title: Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE EXECUTIVE COORDINATOR - ACE-AJ SECRETARIAT Position Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat Host institution Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda Scope Pan-African / multi-country Reporting ACE-AJ Founding Members, through the governance and hosting arrangements of ACE-AJ and LAF Duty station Kigali,Rwanda,withregularregionaland international engagement Contract Full-time; terms to be specified in the employment contract 1. Institutional Background and Rationale The African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice (ACE-AJ) is a Pan-African platform established to strengthen access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights and people-centred justice across Africa. Its origins lie in a continentally grounded feasibility process undertaken in 2016 through consultations with access-to-justice organisations in Kenya, Sierra Leone, Rwanda, Malawi and South Africa. The feasibility work examined the relevance, scope, sustainability, institutional form and operational requirements of a continental centre and identified the need for a stronger African voice, systematic knowledge exchange, research, learning, capacity development and collaboration among organisations working closest to communities. The feasibility process envisaged the Centre as more than a conventional project or secretariat. It was conceived as a galvanising space for access-to-justice and legal-empowerment actors; a repository of African practice and evidence; a platform for peer learning and exchange; a mechanism for strengthening community-based justice; and a vehicle through which African organisations could develop collective positions and speak with greater coherence on continental and global justice questions. ACE-AJ was officially launched in Kigali, Rwanda, in 2017. Since its establishment, it has evolved into a multi-country network bringing together civil society organisations and justice actors committed to expanding access to justice for poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities. The Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda, is a founding member and hosts the ACE-AJ Secretariat. ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 provides the current institutional roadmap. It organises the Centre’s work around five mutually reinforcing priorities: promoting holistic justice delivery; strengthening capacity building; research and knowledge generation; advocacy and communication; and strengthening the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The Strategy also places substantial emphasis on monitoring, learning, institutional visibility, membership growth, strategic partnerships and diversified resource mobilisation. 2. Purpose and Strategic Character of the Position The Executive Coordinator is the principal executive and operational lead of the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The purpose of the position is to provide disciplined continental coordination and executive leadership for the implementation of ACE-AJ’s Constitution, Strategic Framework 2024–2030, decisions of the General Assembly and Board, approved programmes and institutional commitments. The Executive Coordinator will move ACE-AJ from strategy to implementation. The office holder will connect a geographically dispersed membership, translate strategic priorities into annual and multi-year plans, mobilise resources, coordinate multi-country programmes, strengthen governance and institutional systems, generate and communicate evidence, develop strategic partnerships and position ACE-AJ as a credible African platform on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. The position therefore requires a network builder and institutional entrepreneur, not only a programme administrator. The Executive Coordinator must combine continental vision with implementation discipline; diplomacy with accountability; strong member relations with external representation; and programme leadership with fundraising, knowledge generation and organisational development. 3. Overall Accountability Serve as the principal executive focal point for implementation of ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 and approved annual priorities. Ensure that decisions of the General Assembly and Board are translated into clear workstreams, responsibilities, timelines, budgets, deliverables and measurable results. Lead the day-to-day work of the Secretariat and coordinate Secretariat personnel, consultants, technical advisers and designated support from member organisations. Maintain effective operational coordination with LAF as host institution while safeguarding ACE-AJ’s distinct continental identity, governance and member ownership. Provide timely, evidence-based advice to the Board on institutional development, programme performance, partnerships, funding, risks and emerging access-to-justice trends. 4. Key Responsibilities 4.1 Continental Network Coordination, Membership and Movement Building Provide proactive day-to-day coordination of ACE-AJ as a Pan-African network and maintain substantive engagement with members across countries, regions, legal traditions and languages. Develop an annual member-engagement architecture covering consultations, focal-person meetings, peer exchanges, communities of practice, thematic working groups, institutional visits and regional or continental convenings. Maintain structured two-way communication between the Secretariat, Board, General Assembly, founding members, and strategic partners. Map and continuously update member expertise, innovations, community-justice models, research, policy experience, institutional capacities and support needs. Strengthen member ownership by creating practical opportunities for members to lead research, training, advocacy, convening and cross-country initiatives. Lead strategic membership growth, with particular attention to geographic balance and stronger representation from underrepresented parts of the continent. Coordinate membership admission, onboarding, orientation, retention and an accurate, functional membership database. Identify common challenges across jurisdictions and convert them into collective learning, research, advocacy and programme initiatives. 4.2 Strategy Implementation and Institutional Performance Translate the 2024–2030 Strategic Framework into costed annual work plans, implementation matrices, institutional calendars and measurable performance commitments. Coordinate implementation across all five strategic priorities and ensure that programme choices remain connected to ACE-AJ’s mission, comparative advantage and member experience. Develop a Secretariat performance dashboard showing progress against strategic outcomes, programme commitments, membership engagement, partnerships, fundraising, visibility and governance decisions. Institute quarterly implementation reviews and prepare concise performance briefs for the Board. Identify implementation bottlenecks, emerging risks and opportunities and recommend corrective measures. Coordinate periodic strategy reviews and contribute evidence for the development of ACE-AJ’s post-2030 strategic direction. 4.3 Holistic and People-Centred Justice Advance ACE-AJ’s agenda on holistic justice delivery by connecting formal, informal and community-based justice actors and approaches. Promote recognition of community-based justice practitioners and strengthen their contribution to accessible, affordable and responsive justice systems. Support member initiatives that demonstrate how legal empowerment, mediation, community justice, legal aid and other people-centred approaches can complement formal justice institutions. Facilitate cross-country learning on enabling policy and regulatory environments for community-based justice and paralegal practice. Ensure that the perspectives of poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities remain central to ACE-AJ’s programmes, research, advocacy and institutional narrative. 4.4 Capacity Building and Peer Learning Develop and coordinate a continental capacity-building programme informed by member needs and the Strategy. Organise practical peer-to-peer learning, mentorship, technical exchanges and cross-country exposure among members. Develop partnerships with universities, legal aid clinics, professional bodies, judiciaries and specialist institutions for training, research and professional development. Promote learning models that draw systematically on the experience of ACE-AJ members rather than relying exclusively on external expertise. Support development of scalable training resources and, where feasible, longer and more intensive learning programmes for community-based justice practitioners. 4.5 Research, Evidence and Knowledge Management Lead implementation of ACE-AJ’s research and knowledge-generation agenda, including practitioner-driven and comparative research with continental policy relevance. Coordinate documentation of best practices, innovations, impact case studies and lessons from member organisations. Develop and maintain an accessible knowledge-sharing platform or e-repository for research, laws, policies, tools, case studies and member resources. Promote common or compatible data-collection approaches across members to strengthen the African evidence base on access to justice. Coordinate research partnerships with universities, research institutions and practitioners and ensure appropriate ethical, data-protection and quality standards. Translate research into policy briefs, position papers, learning products, advocacy messages and practical tools for members and decision-makers. 4.6 Continental Advocacy, Policy Influence and Representation Develop and coordinate ACE-AJ’s continental advocacy agenda, drawing on member evidence and experience. Support development of coherent African positions on legal empowerment, community justice, legal aid, people-centred justice and related emerging issues. Build structured engagement with the African Union, African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights, regional economic communities, United Nations mechanisms and other relevant regional and global institutions. Identify opportunities for ACE-AJ and its members to contribute to justice-sector reform, policy processes, legislative discussions and international forums. Represent ACE-AJ at authorised regional, continental and international engagements and prepare high-quality briefs, statements and speaking points. Ensure that ACE-AJ’s advocacy elevates member expertise and community experience rather than substituting for them. 4.7 Strategic Communication, Visibility and African Narrative Lead implementation of an institutional communication and visibility plan that establishes ACE-AJ as a recognised source of African expertise on access to justice and legal empowerment. Oversee regular member updates, newsletters, website content, social media, publications and other institutional communication. Develop a compelling evidence-based continental narrative demonstrating ACE-AJ’s added value and the contribution of its members. Increase dissemination and citation of ACE-AJ research, policy products and member-generated knowledge. Coordinate media engagement and ensure consistent branding, messaging and recognition of member organisations. 4.8 Resource Mobilisation and Financial Sustainability Develop, maintain and drive a diversified resource-mobilisation strategy and funding pipeline aligned with ACE-AJ’s strategic priorities. Map foundations, bilateral and multilateral partners, international organisations, corporate and philanthropic actors and other potential supporters. Lead or coordinate high-quality concept notes, proposals, budgets, partnership submissions and donor presentations. Build and maintain long-term donor and strategic-partner relationships and coordinate due diligence, negotiations, stewardship and reporting. Explore sustainable non-grant income approaches consistent with ACE-AJ’s mandate, governance and applicable legal requirements. Work with the host institution and relevant governance structures to ensure sound grant management, financial controls, compliance and transparent reporting. Strengthen ACE-AJ’s ability to demonstrate impact as a central element of fundraising and partnership development. 4.9 Programme Development, Multi-country Implementation and Accountability Design and coordinate multi-country and network-wide initiatives from concept development through implementation, monitoring, learning and reporting. Develop clear implementation arrangements with participating members, including roles, deliverables, budgets, timelines, reporting requirements and decision-making arrangements. Track delivery across countries and intervene early where implementation is delayed or quality is at risk. Coordinate narrative and management reporting to the Board, members, partners and donors. Ensure programmes demonstrate clear value to participating members and contribute to ACE-AJ’s strategic outcomes rather than operating as isolated projects. 4.10 Governance and Institutional Development Provide high-quality technical and administrative support to the Board and General Assembly. Coordinate AGMs, Board meetings and other governance processes, including agendas, briefing papers, minutes, decision registers and systematic follow-up. Maintain constitutional, governance, membership, programme and institutional records. Support development, review and implementation of policies, manuals, procedures and internal systems required for a credible continental institution. Ensure Secretariat operations comply with the ACE-AJ Constitution, approved policies, governance decisions and relevant legal and contractual obligations. Support the establishment and effective operation of thematic working groups, committees, patrons or other mechanisms provided for in ACE-AJ’s strategic and governance framework. 5. Expected Results and Performance Indicators ACE-AJ functions as an active, connected and member-owned continental network with demonstrably regular and substantive member participation. Annual strategic priorities and governance decisions are implemented, tracked and reported systematically. Membership expands strategically and becomes more geographically and linguistically representative. Regional and continental exchanges, working groups and joint initiatives produce documented learning and collaborative action. ACE-AJ generates and disseminates credible African evidence, research, best practices and policy products. ACE-AJ’s visibility and participation in relevant African and international justice platforms increases. A credible and diversified funding pipeline is maintained, with stronger donor stewardship and institutional sustainability. Multi-country programmes demonstrate timely delivery, accountability, learning and clear value to participating members. Governance, programme, financial, membership, partnership and communication records are accurate, current and accessible. ACE-AJ increasingly contributes an identifiable African voice to debates and policy processes on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. 6. Qualifications and Experience Master’s degree in law, Human Rights, Development Studies, Public Policy, International Relations, Governance, Programme Management or a closely related field. A strong bachelor’s degree combined with substantial relevant senior experience may be considered. At least 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights, governance, civil society strengthening, international development, network leadership or a closely related field. Demonstrated experience coordinating a network, coalition, secretariat, regional platform or multi-country partnership. Substantial experience working across several African countries is strongly preferred. Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into implementation plans, budgets, partnerships, programmes and measurable results. Strong experience in programme design and management, monitoring and learning, budgeting, reporting and institutional planning. Proven experience in resource mobilisation, proposal development and donor or strategic-partner relationship management. Experience supporting governance bodies and organisational/institutional development. Experience in research, policy engagement, advocacy, knowledge management or capacity development relevant to access to justice is highly desirable. Excellent written and spoken English. Working knowledge of French is a strong advantage; knowledge of other widely used African languages is an asset. 7. Core Competencies and Leadership Profile Continental network leadership and movement building. Strategic execution and disciplined follow-through. Member engagement, coalition management and cross-cultural diplomacy. Resource mobilisation, partnership development and donor stewardship. Programme leadership and multi-country coordination. Governance, institutional development and accountability. Research literacy, evidence use and knowledge translation. High-level writing, communication, advocacy and representation. Sound judgement, political and institutional sensitivity, integrity and independence. Ability to work effectively across borders, time zones, institutions and professional cultures with limited supervision. 8. Particular Profile Sought ACE-AJ is seeking an Executive Coordinator who can build an institution and a continental network at the same time. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging organisational leaders, practitioners, community-justice actors, academics, donors, governments, regional institutions and international partners. The person must be able to create trust among members while maintaining delivery discipline and accountability. Candidates should demonstrate through concrete examples how they have coordinated networks or multi-country partnerships; converted strategy into implementation; maintained active member participation; handled competing institutional interests; mobilised resources; built strategic partnerships; convened diverse actors; generated or used evidence for policy influence; and contributed to institutional growth, visibility and sustainability. 9. Reporting, Supervision and Working Relationships The Executive Coordinator shall report to the ACE-AJ Founding Members in accordance with the Constitution and shall operate within the agreed hosting arrangements with LAF. The Executive Coordinator will work closely with the Chairperson and other Board members, the General Assembly, member organisations and designated focal persons. For hosted administrative functions, the Executive Coordinator will maintain close operational coordination with the Executive Director and relevant departments of LAF. The Executive Coordinator will supervise ACE-AJ Secretariat personnel and coordinate consultants, technical advisers, interns, service providers and staff designated by member organisations to support ACE-AJ activities, subject to approved structures and budgets. 10. Eligibility and Right to Work in Rwanda This recruitment is primarily intended for Rwandan nationals and non-Rwandan nationals who are already legally resident in Rwanda and authorised to work in Rwanda. Due to the resources available for this position, ACE-AJ/LAF will not provide international relocation, expatriate benefits, or sponsorship for relocation to Rwanda. Applicants must therefore be able to take up the position in Kigali under an existing lawful right to reside and work in Rwanda. 11. Application Requirements Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae, a letter of motivation, copies of relevant degree(s) and certificate(s), and two professional references. The motivation letter should specifically demonstrate experience in coordinating networks, coalitions or multi-country partnerships and provide concrete examples of continental or cross-country coordination, strategy implementation, convening, membership engagement, partnership development and resource mobilisation. Applications should be addressed to the Executive Director of LAF, as host of the ACE-AJ Secretariat, and submitted by email to legalaidrwanda@gmail.com with a copy (cc) to ace.a2j@gmail.com The deadline for submission of applications is 30 October 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

Guest Experience & Journey Delivery Welcome guests warmly and professionally at airports, hotels, lodges and other meeting points, assisting with luggage and ensuring an excellent first impression. Provide safe, comfortable and punctual transportation for airport transfers, day tours and multi-day journeys throughout Rwanda. Take ownership of the guest experience throughout each journey, providing attentive and highly personalised service. Know each itinerary thoroughly, including timings, activities, accommodation, inclusions and important guest requirements. Coordinate closely with lodges, park offices, activity providers and the Sambora operations team to ensure seamless journey delivery. Stay informed about scheduled activities and any changes on the ground so guests are always well briefed. Anticipate guest needs, including dietary, comfort and accessibility requirements. Recommend appropriate stops for refreshments, meals, photography, viewpoints and rest along the journey. Adapt professionally to weather, road conditions, delays or changing guest needs, communicating proactively with the operations team before making significant itinerary changes. Identify guest concerns early and work calmly and professionally with the operations team to resolve them. 2. Guiding & Interpretation Provide engaging, accurate and thoughtful interpretation of Rwanda's history, culture, communities, conservation, wildlife, birdlife and landscapes. Conduct Kigali and other city tours, cultural visits, scenic journeys and game drives to a consistently high standard. Spot, identify and interpret wildlife and birdlife while ensuring respectful and responsible wildlife viewing. Brief guests thoroughly before activities such as gorilla and chimpanzee trekking, including what to expect, park regulations and what to bring. Continually develop your knowledge of Rwanda, its destinations, history, wildlife, conservation and contemporary life. Adapt your guiding and communication style to different guests, recognising when guests want conversation and interpretation and when they prefer privacy or quiet. Promote responsible tourism by respecting communities, wildlife, national parks and the environment and encouraging guests to do the same. 3. Guest Care & Professional Conduct Build warm but professional relationships with guests while maintaining appropriate boundaries and discretion. Respond to questions, requests and concerns calmly, confidently and professionally. Maintain complete guest confidentiality and respect the privacy of every traveller. Never photograph, film or post guests, their movements or their itineraries publicly without appropriate permission. Understand journey inclusions and arrangements and avoid discussing confidential company rates, commissions or commercial agreements with guests or suppliers. Maintain an excellent standard of personal presentation and represent Sambora professionally at all times. 4. Safe & Professional Driving Operate Sambora's 4x4 safari and touring vehicles safely, smoothly and responsibly. Follow Rwandan traffic laws, national park regulations and Sambora's safety procedures at all times. Maintain defensive driving practices on highways, urban roads, gravel roads, mountain routes and off-road park tracks. Plan routes carefully and allow sufficient time for traffic, weather, road conditions, park or border checkpoints and scheduled activities. Never drive while impaired by alcohol, drugs, medication, fatigue or any other condition that could compromise guest safety. Immediately report accidents, vehicle damage, incidents, near misses or safety concerns. Administer basic first aid when required and follow Sambora's emergency procedures. 5. Vehicle Care & Readiness Present a spotlessly clean, organised and guest-ready vehicle before every guest movement. Ensure vehicles are appropriately stocked with drinking water, reference materials, binoculars, first aid supplies and other required guest amenities. Complete required pre-departure and daily vehicle inspections, including tyres, lights, brakes, oil, coolant, fuel or charge level, windows, safety equipment and other essential components. Operate pop-up roofs and other safari vehicle equipment correctly and safely. Report mechanical faults, warning lights, unusual vehicle behaviour, damage or maintenance requirements immediately. Treat company vehicles responsibly and take reasonable steps to prevent avoidable damage. Ensure required vehicle documents, permits and insurance documentation are valid and available. 6. Communication, Administration & Reporting Maintain regular and proactive communication with the Sambora operations team throughout each journey. Maintain accurate trip, mileage, fuel or charging, vehicle and expense records and submit them on time. Manage park documentation, permits, vouchers and other tour documentation as assigned. Maintain receipts and supporting documentation for company expenditure. Complete trip reports following journeys, including relevant guest feedback, incidents, operational observations and suggestions for improvement. Use WhatsApp, navigation applications and Sambora's digital systems confidently for operational communication and reporting. Support other touring and operational responsibilities when reasonably required. Qualifications & Experience We are looking for candidates who can demonstrate both excellent guiding ability and professional driving standards. Minimum three years' relevant experience as a tour guide driver, safari guide or in a comparable tourism role. Valid Rwandan driving licence appropriate for the vehicles operated. Proven experience driving 4x4 vehicles and confidence on rough, gravel and off-road terrain. Excellent spoken English and Kinyarwanda, with the confidence and vocabulary to engage naturally with international guests. French, German or another international language is a strong advantage. Excellent knowledge of Rwanda's national parks, destinations, road network, history, culture, wildlife and tourism experiences. Certificate or diploma in tourism, tour guiding or hospitality is an advantage. Relevant RDB tour guide certification is preferred. Valid first aid certification, or willingness to undertake certification. Basic understanding of vehicle maintenance, warning signs and routine vehicle inspections. Comfortable using smartphones, digital navigation, WhatsApp and electronic reporting systems. The Person We're Looking For Qualifications and experience matter, but so does personality. You should be: A natural host who genuinely enjoys looking after people. An engaging storyteller with curiosity and a desire to keep learning. Warm and personable without being intrusive. Able to read guests and adapt your approach to different personalities, cultures and expectations. Calm and resourceful when plans change or problems arise. Safety-conscious and disciplined behind the wheel. Reliable, punctual and highly organised. Discreet and respectful of guest privacy. Proud to represent Rwanda and passionate about sharing the country with visitors. Comfortable working flexible hours and spending extended periods away from Kigali, including weekends and public holidays. How Success Will Be Measured Performance in this role will include: Consistently strong guest feedback on guiding, driving, knowledge and service. Accurate, engaging and appropriate guiding and interpretation. Safe and responsible driving, with no preventable incidents attributable to unsafe driving or failure to follow procedures. Consistently punctual pick-ups, transfers and activity arrivals. Successful delivery of itineraries and proactive communication when circumstances change. Exceptional vehicle cleanliness, presentation and guest readiness. Timely identification and reporting of vehicle faults, damage and maintenance requirements. Accurate and timely operational, mileage, fuel/charging and expense reporting. Professional conduct, presentation and communication. Positive collaboration with colleagues, lodges, activity providers, park authorities and other partners. What We Offer A competitive salary reflecting experience, qualifications and skills. A daily per diem for every day spent on tour. Meals while on duty. Comprehensive medical insurance. Monthly transport and communication allowance. Training and opportunities to continue developing your guiding, destination and professional skills. The opportunity to join a growing Rwandan hospitality and private travel company committed to delivering exceptional experiences and showcasing Rwanda at its very best. How To Apply Apply via the Jobs in Rwanda website or by emailing careers@samborakinigi.com . Ensure you submit a cover letter explaining why you are the right candidate, as well as a copy of your CV. Deadline: 13 October 2026 Apply

raw_text: CHAI RWANDA VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT Title: Associate, Data Scientist Program: Health Systems Strengthening Job Location: Kigali, Rwanda Type: Full-Time Paid Start date: Immediate Overview The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. Programs Overview The Government of Rwanda (GoR) strives to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by enabling equitable access to quality health services for the population as outlined in the Fourth Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP IV). This commitment has been made against a backdrop of rising health care costs and uncertainty around the future availability of donor funding and calls for improved health sector sustainability. Acknowledging this, the Government aims to employ effective, equitable, efficient, and sustainable health care financing and systems strengthening, putting an emphasis on primary health care as the cornerstone of a strong and sustainable health system. CHAI Rwanda’s Health System Strengthening (HSS) programs work on a day-to-day basis with Government leadership in the Ministry of Health (MoH) and the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB). The goal of those programs is to support the Government to accelerate progress towards UHC by ensuring the sustainable delivery of quality, essential health services. This includes designing and implementing national Primary Health Care (PHC) reforms from health center level down to community health, to increase health workforce availability, to prioritize and sustainably finance essential services, and to support improved management, financing, and delivery of quality primary health care. Position overview CHAI currently seeks an Associate Data Scientist to work with the Ministry of Health (MOH), reporting directly to the head of data science at the National Health Intelligence Center to help improve the quality, governance, and use of evidence on policy decision making. S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI supported initiatives. The Associate Data Scientist is responsible for leading advanced data analytics, statistical modeling, and applied machine learning across priority public health and clinical domains. The role ensures that health data is transformed into high-quality, reliable, explainable, and decision-ready intelligence that informs AI development, policy decisions, and health system performance improvement. This role serves as the technical bridge between raw health data, AI models, and real-world decision-making, ensuring scientific rigor, reproducibility, and national-scale usability. This is a top government priority for MOH, and the Associate, Data Scientist will therefore be seconded to the MOH/NHIC, S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI-supported initiatives. Job responsibilities: The key functions and deliverables of this role will include: Advanced Data Analytics and Statistical Modeling Lead advanced descriptive, predictive, and inferential analyses across clinical, surveillance, and health systems datasets. Develop and validate predictive models, risk stratification algorithms, forecasting models, epidemiological and operational analytics Apply rigorous statistical methods, hypothesis testing, and causal inference techniques to support decision-making. Ensure all analytics are clinically interpretable, policy-relevant, and scientifically defensible. Feature Engineering & Machine Learning Support Design robust feature engineering pipelines from EMRs, HMIS, LMIS and surveillance platforms Support AI Engineers with high-quality training datasets, feature selection, bias detection and data representativeness testing Contribute to development of machine learning models, particularly in tabular health data, time-series forecasting and population-level risk prediction. Data Quality, Governance and Integrity Lead implementation of data quality frameworks, completeness, consistency, accuracy and timeliness checks Perform data audits, outlier detection, bias and missing data analysis Ensure compliance with national health data governance standards, privacy and ethical data use policies. Maintain full data documentation, metadata standards, and lineage tracking. Health Systems Intelligence & Decision Support Develop decision-support analytics and public health dashboards for disease burden tracking, resource allocation and service delivery optimization. Translate analytical outputs into policy briefs, executive dashboards, technical report. Ensure outputs are actionable, explainable, and aligned with the national health priorities. Data Engineering Support and Pipeline optimization Work closely with Data engineers, integration teams and AI engineers to ensure analytics assets are scalable, reproducible and production ready. Support data pipeline optimization, ETL quality validation and real-time and batch processing readiness Mentorship, Capacity Building & Collaboration Mentor junior data scientists and analysts Lead internal analytics communities of practice, code reviews and methodology workshops Serve as a technical reviewer for analytics protocols, research designs and data science deliverables Innovation and Continuous Improvement Stay current with advances in Machine Learning, Statistical Science, Health Analytics, Artificial Intelligence and Causal Inference trends Propose innovative analytics and data science use cases for public health, service delivery, health financing, supply chain and logistics for pharmaceuticals and disease surveillance Required Qualifications MSc degree in relevant discipline (Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Operations Research, Statistics, Epidemiology, Health Informatics) 5-8 years of professional experience in the field of advanced analytics and/or applied statistics preferably with Data Science applications Solid mathematical foundation and knowledge of a variety of statistical methods (e.g. regression, classification, clustering, experimental design, modeling, advanced forecasting) Proven experience working with large-scale datasets, regulated data environments, preferably within a health domain. Strong proficiency in data visualization, demonstrated experience in Python, R, SQL, and working with structured, semi-structured and unstructured datasets Ability to focus on vaguely defined problems requiring the application of a creative approach. Strong teamworking skills Excellent written and verbal communication skills for coordinating across teams. Ability to mentor and lead teams in a fast-paced and changing environment.
