raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToR) FOR THE RECRUITMENT OF THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR Position: Executive DirectorDuty Station: Kigali, Rwanda, Reports to: Chairperson of the Board of DirectorsSupervisory Authority: Board of Directors 1. BACKGROUND AND JUSTIFICATION Association Rwandaise des Conseillers en Traumatisme (ARCT-RUHUKA) is a national non-governmental organisation of professional trauma counsellors established in 1998. The organization evolved from a trauma counselling programme implemented with the support of Trócaire, an Irish charity organisation, in response to the need for trauma counselling and psychosocial support in Rwanda. ARCT-RUHUKA was subsequently formally established and obtained legal recognition as a non-governmental organisation under Ministerial Decree No. 97/11 of 28 July 2007. The organization was later legally registered with the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB) under Legal Personality No. 97/11 dated 12 September 2013. In accordance with the applicable legal and regulatory framework, ARCT-RUHUKA has continued to maintain its legal compliance and institutional standing. Its most recent certificate, issued by the Rwanda Governance Board on 30 September 2026, certifies that Association Rwandaise des Conseillers en Traumatisme (ARCT-RUHUKA), a national non-governmental organization with Legal Personality No. 97/11 of 12 September 2013, complies with Law No. 058/2024 of 20 June 2024 and the related regulations. Over the years, ARCT-RUHUKA has evolved into an established national organisation dedicated to trauma counselling, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), professional capacity development, advocacy, institutional strengthening, and child rights and protection. Through its qualified and committed staff, the organisation works across various sectors and communities in Rwanda, providing technical expertise, professional support, and integrated services that promote mental well-being, strengthen resilience, protect vulnerable populations, and improve the overall well-being of individuals, families, and communities To strengthen its governance, operational efficiency, institutional sustainability, and impact on target populations, ARCT-RUHUKA seeks to recruit a qualified and experienced Executive Director with strong leadership, strategic management, program coordination, resource mobilization, and organizational development skills. The Executive Director will be responsible for the overall day-to-day management of the organization, implementation of decisions made by statutory organs, coordination of staff and programs, development of strategic partnerships, and achievement of institutional objectives in accordance with the organization's mission, vision, statutes, policies, and procedures. 2. OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION Under the direct supervision of the Chairperson of the Board of Directors and in accordance with the guidance and decisions of the General Assembly and the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will provide strategic leadership and operational management of ARCT-RUHUKA. The Executive Director will ensure effective governance, institutional performance, program quality, resource mobilization, sound human and financial resource management, and the long-term sustainability of the organization. 3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES 3.1. Strategic Leadership and Institutional Governance The Executive Director shall: Provide overall leadership and management to ensure that ARCT-RUHUKA remains an efficient, effective, transparent, and accountable institution; Translate the strategic directions and decisions of the General Assembly and Board of Directors into operational plans and actionable activities; Coordinate the development, review, and implementation of the organization's strategic plan and operational plans, involving all relevant departments and institutional organs; Submit strategic plans, operational plans, budgets, and institutional reports to the Board of Directors for review and approval; Ensure compliance with the organization's statutes, internal regulations, administrative and financial procedures manual, and other institutional policies; Ensure the effective functioning of the organizational structure and propose improvements to strengthen institutional efficiency; Coordinate the preparation of Board of Directors and General Assembly meetings in collaboration with the Chairperson, including agendas, supporting documents, and reports; Ensure timely implementation and follow-up of resolutions, directives, and recommendations from the organization's statutory organs; Propose amendments and improvements to institutional policies, procedures, internal regulations, and other governance documents whenever necessary; Advise the Board of Directors on strategic priorities, institutional risks, development opportunities, and organizational sustainability. 3.2. Administrative and Operational Management The Executive Director shall: Plan, organize, coordinate, supervise, and monitor the day-to-day operations of the Executive Secretariat; Ensure the effective implementation of administrative procedures and internal control systems; Define staff responsibilities and duties in accordance with the approved organizational structure and guidance from the Board of Directors; Ensure effective coordination between departments, decentralized offices, project teams, and operational units; Ensure the availability and efficient utilization of human, material, logistical, and other resources required for the organization's operations; Oversee the management, maintenance, and proper utilization of the organization's assets, infrastructure, equipment, and other property; Strengthen administrative systems, management tools, and internal communication mechanisms; Maintain effective administrative relations with relevant public, private institutions, regulatory authorities, and partners. Identify operational challenges and implement appropriate corrective measures; Ensure business continuity and take immediate action in emergencies within delegated authority, in collaboration with the Board of Directors. 3.3. Program and Project Management The Executive Director shall: Provide overall coordination and supervision of all programs and projects in line with the organization's mission, strategic plan, and contractual obligations; Oversee the development of project proposals, work plans, results frameworks, and budgets in collaboration with program managers and relevant departments; Ensure the technical quality, relevance, efficiency, effectiveness, and sustainability of the organization's interventions; Ensure that programs respond to the needs of beneficiaries and uphold the principles of dignity, confidentiality, safeguarding, and non-discrimination; Coordinate the implementation of training, trauma counselling, clinical supervision, psychosocial support, awareness-raising, and advocacy activities; Ensure that project activities are implemented according to approved timelines, budgets, performance indicators, and expected results; Promote complementarity and synergies among the organization's programs and projects; Organize regular coordination and performance review meetings with staff. Ensure that recommendations from evaluations, audits, monitoring visits, and partner reviews are addressed and implemented; Promote innovation, institutional learning, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement in program quality. 3.4. Financial Management, Budgeting, and Internal Controls In collaboration with the Director of Finance and Administration (DAF), the Executive Director shall: Coordinate the preparation of the organization's consolidated budget and submit it to the Board of Directors for approval; Ensure budget implementation in accordance with approved allocations, donor agreements, and the organization's administrative and financial procedures manual; Regularly monitor budget execution and implement corrective measures to address significant variances; Review and approve financial reports prepared by the Finance and Administration Department before submission to the Board of Directors or partners; Ensure the establishment, maintenance, and effective implementation of internal control systems, risk management mechanisms, and fraud prevention measures; Authorize expenditures, financial commitments, and staff mission orders within the limits of delegated authority; Ensure that financial reports are accurate, reliable, timely, and compliant with statutory, accounting, and donor requirements; Ensure compliance with applicable tax, social security, accounting, and financial regulations; Oversee the preparation and implementation of internal and external audits and ensure timely follow-up of audit recommendations; Promote transparency, accountability, and the efficient utilization of financial and material resources; Ensure compliance with donor-specific financial procedures, grant conditions, and contractual obligations; Support the development of resource diversification and long-term financial sustainability strategies. The Executive Director shall exercise financial authority in accordance with the principles of segregation of duties, dual control, and the organization's approved delegation of authority framework. 3.5. Human Resource Management and Staff Development The Executive Director shall: Implement the organization's human resource management policies in accordance with its statutes, staff regulations, and procedures manual; Identify and plan staffing needs in line with strategic priorities, program requirements, and available resources; Recruit, assign, and supervise permanent and temporary support staff within the limits of delegated authority; Submit proposals for the recruitment of senior management staff and staff termination decisions to the Board of Directors where such decisions fall within its authority; Establish staff performance objectives and conduct regular, transparent, and objective performance appraisals; Promote a professional, inclusive, respectful, and harassment-free working environment; Identify staff capacity-building needs and develop appropriate training and professional development plans; Promote staff motivation, teamwork, accountability, and professional growth; Ensure compliance with applicable labor laws, staff protection policies, and internal procedures; Address workplace conflicts and propose appropriate solutions; Promote succession planning, leadership development, and knowledge transfer within the organization. 3.6. Resource Mobilization, Partnerships, and Institutional Development The Executive Director shall: Develop and submit a resource mobilization and partnership development strategy to the Board of Directors for approval; Identify funding opportunities from bilateral and multilateral donors, United Nations agencies, international NGOs, foundations, and private sector partners; Coordinate the development and submission of project proposals, concept notes, funding applications, and partnership initiatives; Establish, maintain, and strengthen relationships with technical and financial partners, public institutions, civil society organizations, and professional networks; Represent the organization in coordination meetings, forums, platforms, and partnership engagements as delegated; Negotiate partnership opportunities in accordance with the organization's strategic priorities and authorized signing powers; Develop income-generating and self-financing initiatives that are consistent with the organization's mission and statutes; Enhance the visibility, credibility, and institutional positioning of ARCT-RUHUKA; Ensure compliance with funding agreements, contractual commitments, and accountability requirements; Diversify funding sources to reduce dependence on a limited number of donors and strengthen institutional sustainability. 3.7. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning The Executive Director shall: Establish and maintain an integrated system for institutional planning, monitoring, evaluation, reporting, and performance management; Define institutional, programmatic, financial, and administrative performance indicators in collaboration with relevant managers; Supervise the preparation and timely submission of narrative, technical, financial, and institutional reports; Periodically assess progress against operational plans, budgets, and expected results; Organize performance review meetings and ensure follow-up on agreed recommendations; Promote the collection, analysis, and use of reliable data to support evidence-based decision-making; Ensure effective accountability mechanisms for beneficiaries, communities, governance organs, and development partners; Promote knowledge sharing, documentation of good practices, and institutional learning; Oversee the implementation of improvement plans arising from evaluations, audits, and performance reviews. 3.8. Legal Compliance, Ethics, and Risk Management The Executive Director shall: Ensure compliance with the organization's statutes, internal regulations, and applicable laws and regulations governing non-profit organizations in Rwanda; Ensure that the organization meets its legal, administrative, and regulatory obligations to relevant authorities; Coordinate the preparation, maintenance, and updating of legal, administrative, and institutional documents; Ensure the implementation of policies on fraud prevention, anti-corruption, safeguarding, and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse; Identify institutional, financial, operational, legal, and reputational risks and propose appropriate mitigation measures; 0Ensure the protection of personal data, confidentiality of information, and adherence to professional standards in trauma counselling; Coordinate the management of legal matters and disputes in collaboration with the Board of Directors and, where necessary, a legal advisor; Ensure that legal representation and judicial proceedings are conducted in accordance with statutory requirements and the authority delegated by the Board of Directors. 3.9. Institutional Communication and Representation The Executive Director shall: Ensure effective institutional communication within the organization and with external stakeholders; Represent ARCT-RUHUKA in civil, administrative, and partnership matters within the limits of the authority granted; Maintain professional relationships with government authorities, development partners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders; Oversee the preparation and dissemination of institutional reports, publications, and communication materials; Promote the organization's image, visibility, and reputation in line with its mission, vision, and ethical principles; Submit significant matters requiring strategic decisions or specific representation to the Board of Directors 4. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND PROFILE 4.1. Academic Qualifications The candidate shall: Hold at least a Master's degree or equivalent in Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Mental Health, Psychosocial Support, Social Work, Public Health, Administration, Management, Sociology, Community Development, Development Studies, Project Management, or another relevant field aligned with ARCT-RUHUKA's programmes and strategic objectives. Possess relevant professional experience in trauma counselling, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), child protection, community development, advocacy, institutional capacity building, or the management of non-governmental organisations. Demonstrate proven experience in strategic leadership, organisational management, programme planning, project implementation, resource mobilisation, and donor relations. Have a strong understanding of NGO governance, financial management, human resource management, partnership development, and institutional sustainability. 4.2. Professional Experience The candidate shall demonstrate: At least five (5) years of relevant professional experience in organizational, program, or project management; At least five (5) years of experience in a managerial, leadership, or supervisory position; Practical experience in program coordination, administrative and financial management, strategic planning, and human resource management; Experience managing projects funded by national or international development partners; Experience in the design, development, or implementation of trauma counselling, mental health, or psychosocial support programs shall be a significant advantage; Experience in resource mobilization, partnership development, and institutional management shall be an added advantage. Demonstrate experience working with Community on special attention to vulnerable people , including survivors of trauma, women, children, adolescents, and other at-risk groups. 4.3. Technical Competencies The candidate shall demonstrate: Strong knowledge of strategic and operational planning; Solid skills in program and project management, budgeting, and financial oversight; Good understanding of internal control systems, risk management, and compliance; Strong competencies in human resource management, leadership, and organizational development; Ability to develop funding proposals and negotiate partnerships; Good knowledge of monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning systems; Familiarity with donor requirements and grant management procedures; Knowledge of laws and regulations applicable to non-profit organizations in Rwanda; Proficiency in computer applications and administrative, financial, and reporting systems. 4.4. Language Requirements Excellent command of English and Kinyarwanda, both written and spoken; Good command of French, written and spoken; 4.5. Personal and Behavioral Competencies The candidate shall demonstrate: Strategic leadership and sound decision-making skills; Integrity, honesty, transparency, and high ethical standards; Excellent communication, negotiation, and representation skills; Teamwork and the ability to work in multicultural environments; Strong organizational skills, initiative, and the ability to manage competing priorities; Problem-solving and conflict management abilities; Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines; Sensitivity to mental health, safeguarding, confidentiality, and human dignity; Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of ARCT-RUHUKA. 4.6. Other Requirements Rwandan nationality, if required by the organization's statutes and applicable regulations; Maximum age 45 years, subject to confirmation of compliance with the organization's statutes and applicable laws; Availability for domestic and occasional international travel; A valid Category B driving license shall be an advantage or a requirement if confirmed by the organization's internal regulations. 5. APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS. Interested candidates shall submit an application dossier comprising: A motivation letter addressed to the Chairperson of the Board of Directors of ARCT-RUHUKA; An updated and detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV); Copies of academic qualifications and relevant training certificates; Employment certificates or other evidence of relevant professional experience; Contact details of three professional referees; A copy of a valid national identity card; Criminal records. Any other relevant supporting documents demonstrating the candidate's qualifications and experience. The application submission procedure, receiving address, and deadline shall be communicated in the official vacancy announcement. The recruitment process shall uphold the principles of transparency, fairness, confidentiality, equal opportunity, merit, and prevention of conflicts of interest. 6. Submission Details Interested and eligible candidates are invited to submit their application documents to the email: arct.recruitment@gmail.com The submission deadline is 22nd October 2026. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. ONLY shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information or clarification, interested candidates may contact ARCT-RUHUKA during official working hours at +250 796 894 484. Done at Kigali, on 04th October 2026. Our mission is to build an accounting firm in Rwanda, and beyond which serves clients on a global level with a specific focus on Rwanda and Switzerland and other selective markets. To learn more about our culture, values and how you can be a part of the team by giving outstanding services to clients globally, please visit us here! https://visionsafrica.com/about-us/ What we offer: Competitive compensation package – RWF220,000 net Guaranteed growth for interested individuals Regular team events, internal trainings and external trainings which are part of our efforts to continuously learn and improve Medical insurance for you and up to 3 dependents (As defined in the Employee Handbook) Paid Time-Off (As defined in the Employee Handbook) Performance Bonus What we’re looking for: As an Accounting Intern, you have the unique opportunity to engage with clients from diverse cultures and backgrounds, becoming an integral part of our global team. Our international reach, spanning Africa, Europe, and the United States, offers a dynamic environment where you'll develop your accounting skills while gaining exposure to global financial practices. Here’s what you can expect: International Accountant: You'll be exposed to a wide range of financial practices across different continents, enhancing your expertise in international accounting. Finance Professional: Immerse yourself in the fundamentals of bookkeeping, accounts payable, and accounts receivable. Numbers Specialist: You will master the intricacies of maintaining general ledger and bank accounts, ensuring seamless financial operations. Your attention to detail will be key to achieving balance and accuracy in all financial records. Financial Reporting Expert: You'll refine your skills in preparing detailed and accurate financial reports. Your work will turn complex financial data into insightful narratives that meet the highest standards. Payroll Specialist: Take charge of payroll processing with precision and reliability. Your role will be crucial in ensuring timely and accurate salary payments for our clients, reflecting your ability to handle this critical responsibility with professionalism. Master of Organization: Your organizational skills will be put to the test as you efficiently collect, update, and maintain financial files. Your ability to bring order to complex data will be a valued asset in maintaining our high standards of record-keeping. This internship is designed to be a transformative experience, equipping you with the skills and knowledge necessary to excel in the accounting field. Key Responsibilities: Accounting Support: Assist with bookkeeping, accounts payable/receivable, payroll processing, and general ledger maintenance. Tax Compliance: Support the preparation and filing of tax returns, ensuring adherence to relevant tax laws and regulations. Client Interaction: Build and maintain positive relationships with clients by assisting with inquiries and providing timely updates. Service Quality Improvement: Participate in training sessions and internal reviews to enhance service quality and accounting practices. Billing and Collections: Assist with the billing process and help manage accounts receivable to ensure timely collections. Customization of Services: Work with senior team members to tailor accounting services to meet specific client needs, enhancing client satisfaction. Support Strategic Initiatives: Contribute to the development of new service offerings, aligning with business needs and personal interests. Research and Documentation: Conduct research on accounting and tax topics, and assist in developing memos, best practices, and training materials. Financial Reporting: Assist in the preparation of accurate financial reports, providing insights to support decision-making. Special Assignments: Contribute to special projects and assignments, ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time. Industry Knowledge: Stay informed on industry trends, tax laws, and best practices to support continuous learning and improvement. About You: A Passion for Numbers: A bachelor's degree in accounting or business will be your entry ticket to this world of opportunities. Tech Savvy: Excel at using Microsoft Office products - your computer skills will make you a wizard in the digital realm. Team Player: Embrace challenges and enjoy collaborating with others. Your teamwork will be the secret to our collective success. Communication Pro: Strong communication and organizational skills will help you navigate smoothly through any task. Attention to Detail: Your impeccable attention to detail will ensure that nothing slips through the cracks. Math & Analytics Whiz: Your strong math and analytical skills will make you an invaluable asset to our team.Career Development Plan: As an Accounting Intern, your initial focus will be on mastering core accounting functions such as bookkeeping, payroll processing, and financial reporting. You will develop proficiency in accounting software and gain exposure to international accounting standards and Rwandan taxation. As you progress, you'll take on more complex tasks, such as managing general ledger accounts and preparing financial statements. You'll begin to engage directly with clients, building relationships and contributing to problem-solving. You'll also start mentoring junior staff and leading smaller projects, developing your leadership and project management skills. Over time, you will establish yourself as a team leader, with responsibilities for building and managing a team, and developing specialized expertise in specific industries or service areas. Your goal will be to become a recognized leader within the organization, contributing to business growth through client engagement, innovation, and mentoring future talent. raw_text: JOB DESCRIPTION FOR THE CLINICAL FIELD SUPERVISOR Location: Ministry of Health, Kigali, Rwanda (with occasional travel to project sites) Reports To: Research Coordinator Contract Type: Full-time Duration: Three (3) years Position Overview: The Ministry of Health, in collaboration with partners, is implementing the research project titled “Evaluating Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Nutrition and Health (MNCNH) Innovation Impact in Rwanda.” The project supports the Health Sector Strategic Plan V (HSSP V, 2024–2029) and evaluates high-impact maternal and neonatal health interventions, including Multiple Micronutrient Supplementation (MMS), Calcium Supplementation, Intravenous Iron, PPH Bundles, and Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS). We are seeking two qualified and motivated Clinical Field Supervisors to oversee clinical and operational activities related to capacity building, field supervision, and quality assurance of study implementation across selected health facilities. The successful candidates will ensure adherence to study protocols, national clinical guidelines, and ethical standards while strengthening facility-level competencies in maternal, neonatal, and child health services. The position will be seconded to the Ministry of Health. Key Responsibilities Conduct regular supervisory visits to assigned hospitals and health centers to ensure compliance with clinical protocols, study procedures, and national guidelines. Monitor fidelity to implementation of study interventions, including MMS, calcium supplementation, IV iron administration, PPH management bundles, and POCUS. Identify gaps in clinical documentation, case management processes, and quality-of-care indicators, and support facilities through mentorship and on-site coaching. Support training and continuous professional development of healthcare providers on study interventions and data reporting requirements. Facilitate learning sessions, case reviews, and feedback meetings to promote knowledge sharing and continuous quality improvement. Ensure timely documentation and reporting of adverse events, protocol deviations, and study-related incidents in line with research and ethical requirements. Collaborate with data managers and the Research Coordinator to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency of clinical data. Serve as the focal point of communication between field sites and the central project coordination team, ensuring effective follow-up and problem resolution. Contribute to the analysis and interpretation of maternal and neonatal health data to inform implementation improvements. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Medicine and Surgery, Nursing, Midwifery, Public Health, or a related field. A Master’s degree in Medicine, Public Health, Epidemiology, or a related field is an added advantage. Valid professional license to practice in Rwanda is an added advantage. Proven experience in maternal health projects, research, or clinical program implementation. Strong familiarity with Rwanda’s health system, Ministry of Health structures, and national data reporting mechanisms. Demonstrated experience mentoring and supporting healthcare providers in data quality, clinical documentation, and protocol adherence. Experience coordinating field-based health sector activities. Skills & Competencies Strong clinical knowledge in maternal, neonatal, and child health care. Proficiency in Electronic Medical Records (EMR) systems and digital data collection tools. Excellent analytical, organizational, and documentation skills with high attention to detail. Effective communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills to engage multidisciplinary teams. Strong commitment to ethical research practices, patient confidentiality, and professional integrity. Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and travel frequently to field sites. Why Join This Project? Contribute directly to improving the quality of maternal and neonatal health services in Rwanda. Play a key role in strengthening clinical practice and implementation research at facility level. Work closely with national health authorities and multidisciplinary teams on high-impact interventions. Support evidence-based improvements that influence national health policy and practice. raw_text: Position Description: Hospitality ManagerReports To: Managing DirectorDepartment: HospitalityLocation: Hope Haven Rwanda GENERAL POSITION DESCRIPTION: The Hospitality Manager is responsible for ensuring that guests and visitors to Hope Haven’s campuses receive a welcoming, professional, and high-quality experience from arrival through departure. The position provides overall leadership to the Hospitality Team and is responsible for the day-to-day coordination of guest accommodation, meals, schedules, special requests, and hospitality services. The Hospitality Manager works closely with the Managing Director, Hospitality Team, Chef, Agriculture Team, and US Hosting Staff to ensure that guest needs are anticipated and handled efficiently. The role requires a mature and confident individual who can work well with people from different backgrounds and personalities, including senior leaders, international visitors, donors, and other important guests. The Hospitality Manager must be able to communicate clearly and professionally in English, remain calm under pressure, and address concerns or difficult situations with good judgment, respect, and professionalism. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Hospitality Leadership and Team Management Lead, supervise, and support the Hospitality Team to ensure consistent and professional service. Organize staff schedules, working hours, days off, and coverage to ensure uninterrupted hospitality services. Set clear expectations for hospitality staff and follow up on performance, attendance, conduct, and service standards. Provide guidance and coaching to staff and address performance or service concerns promptly. Promote teamwork, accountability, respect, and a positive working environment. Handle different personalities and challenging situations professionally while maintaining appropriate boundaries and standards. Ensure staff understand and consistently follow Hope Haven’s hospitality procedures and expectations. 2. Guest Experience and Relationship Management Ensure guests receive a warm, respectful, professional, and well-organized experience throughout their stay. Welcome guests and ensure their needs are understood and appropriately addressed. Regularly review guest schedules and anticipate changes, special requirements, and upcoming activities. Maintain professional communication with guests, including international visitors, donors, partners, and senior leaders. Respond promptly to guest requests, concerns, and special needs and ensure appropriate follow-up. Handle complaints or difficult situations calmly, professionally, and discreetly. Maintain confidentiality and professionalism when dealing with guest information and requests. Coordinate with US Hosting Staff and other relevant teams to ensure guests receive consistent support. Manage and deliver high-quality guest experience by welcoming and touring guests around the campus, introducing them to key facilities, departments, and personnel, and ensuring they feel well received and supported throughout their visit. Develop cross-training and backup capacity within the hospitality team by ensuring that key functions have trained staff who can step in when the primary person is absent or unavailable, including critical roles such as the Chef. 3. Accommodation and Guest Facilities Ensure guest rooms and hospitality facilities are clean, organized, properly equipped, and ready before guests arrive. Conduct regular checks of guest rooms and facilities and address any issues promptly. Ensure hospitality equipment, furniture, keys, and other property are properly safeguarded and maintained. Report maintenance, renovation, replacement, or repair needs to the appropriate supervisor. Ensure the safety and security of guests’ belongings while they are using Hope Haven facilities. Maintain proper control and accountability of hospitality. 4. Meals, Catering, and Guest Dietary Needs Work closely with the Chef to plan and organize appropriate guest menus. Ensure meals are prepared and served on time according to the daily guest schedule. Communicate guest dietary restrictions, allergies, preferences, and special requirements to the Chef and relevant staff. Coordinate with the Agriculture Manager and team regarding food grown for use in the guest kitchen. Monitor the availability and quality of food supplies needed for guest services. Purchase groceries and other hospitality supplies while maintaining quality, cost awareness, and budget discipline. Monitor the use of hospitality supplies to minimize waste and unnecessary expenses. 5. Guest Scheduling and Event Support Regularly monitor guest schedules and communicate changes to the relevant teams. Coordinate hospitality arrangements for school events, meetings, conferences, and special guest activities. Ensure hospitality preparations are completed in advance of scheduled events. Work with other departments to coordinate guest transportation, meals, accommodation, and other hospitality needs when required. Ensure all assigned hospitality responsibilities are completed on time and to an appropriate professional standard. 6. Communication and Coordination Maintain clear, timely, and professional communication with management, staff, guests, and other stakeholders. Communicate confidently and professionally in English, both verbally and in writing. Ensure important guest information and schedule changes are communicated accurately and promptly. Provide regular updates to the Managing Director on hospitality operations, challenges, guest concerns, and outstanding needs. Respond to requests and assigned tasks with urgency and provide clear follow-up on progress or completion. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE Applicants must possess: Bachelor’s degree or relevant professional qualification in Hospitality Management, Hotel Management, Tourism, Business Administration, or a related field. Minimum 3–5 years of relevant experience in hospitality, hotel operations, guest services, accommodation management, catering, or a similar environment. Previous supervisory or management experience is strongly preferred. Experience working with international guests, senior leaders, donors, executives, or other high-profile visitors is an advantage. Demonstrated experience managing a team with different personalities, backgrounds, and levels of experience. Experience in coordinating guest accommodation, meals, events, schedules, and related services. Strong understanding of professional hospitality and customer-service standards. REQUIRED SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES Communication Excellent English communication skills, both spoken and written. Able to communicate clearly, confidently, respectfully, and professionally with guests, staff, and senior leaders. Able to listen carefully, understand guest expectations, and communicate information accurately. Able to handle sensitive or difficult conversations with maturity and professionalism. Leadership and People Management Strong leadership and team-management skills. Confident in giving direction, setting expectations, and holding staff accountable. Able to manage strong personalities and resolve disagreements or challenging situations constructively. Patient, approachable, firm, and fair when dealing with staff. Able to motivate a team and maintain high service standards even under pressure. Hospitality and Customer Service Strong guest-service orientation with a genuine desire to make guests feel welcomed and valued. High attention to detail and strong organizational skills. Able to anticipate guest needs rather than simply respond to requests. Professional appearance, attitude, and conduct. Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills. Able to remain calm, courteous, and solution-focused in stressful situations. Organization and Accountability Able to manage several responsibilities and priorities at the same time. Strong planning and time-management skills. Reliable and able to work independently with limited supervision. Able to follow instructions while also taking appropriate initiative. Strong sense of responsibility for Hope Haven property, equipment, supplies, and guest welfare. Cost-conscious and able to work within an approved budget. PERSONAL QUALITIES The successful candidate should be: Mature and professional. Confident but respectful. Service-oriented and welcoming. Calm under pressure. Flexible and adaptable. Honest and trustworthy. Discreet when handling confidential or sensitive matters. A strong team player. Comfortable working with people from different cultures and backgrounds. Willing to take initiative and solve problems. Committed to maintaining high standards of hospitality and representing Hope Haven professionally. PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS The Hospitality Manager will be expected to ensure that: Guests receive a consistently professional and welcoming experience. Guest rooms, meals, schedules, and hospitality arrangements are prepared accurately and on time. Hospitality staff are well supervised, organized, and accountable. Guest concerns and requests are handled promptly and professionally. Communication with management, staff, and guests is clear and timely. Hospitality resources and budgets are managed responsibly. Hope Haven is represented professionally through the quality of its hospitality services. Duration of the Assignment The employment contract is expected to be an open-ended contract subject to probation of three months. raw_text: JOB OPPORTUNITY Senior Resource Development Manager World Vision is a child-focused Christian humanitarian organization implementing development programmes in 30 Districts of Rwanda. Our interventions in the strategic period of 2026-2030 seek to reach 2.5 million of the most vulnerable children. This is done through programming in Child Protection, Education, Nutrition and WASH, and Poverty Alleviation (Resilience and Livelihoods). World Vision Rwanda seeks to hire a highly qualified, dedicated, and experienced Rwandan national for the role of Senior Resource Development Manager, joining an established and experienced team. This stimulating position incorporates a range of skills and development in multiple areas, allowing for an exciting opportunity for career growth in a dynamic, global organization. It will be based in Kigali at the Head Office and will report to the National Director. Purpose of the position: The Senior Resource Development Manager provides strategic leadership and overall accountability for World Vision Rwanda's resource mobilization and external engagement agenda. The position leads the development and implementation of strategies that secure sustainable and diversified funding, strengthen organizational positioning, and advance strategic relationships that contribute to the achievement of World Vision Rwanda's Strategic Objectives. As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Manager provides organizational leadership on resource acquisition, donor engagement, funding diversification, business development, and market positioning across institutional, private sector, philanthropic, and domestic funding streams. The role ensures that World Vision Rwanda is strategically positioned within the development landscape, influences key stakeholders, and secures the resources required to deliver sustainable impact for vulnerable children, families, and communities. The Manager serves as a principal advisor to the National Director and Senior Leadership Team on donor trends, development financing, external relations, strategic opportunities, and organizational growth priorities. Diversified and sustainable funding portfolio that supports organizational growth, resilience, and long-term impact. Strong alignment between resource acquisition priorities and National Strategy objectives, ensuring resources are directed toward strategic priorities. Enhanced organizational decision-making through timely advisory support on funding opportunities, market trends, and resource mobilization risks. A culture of innovation, accountability, and resource stewardship embedded across the organization, strengthening funding competitiveness and sustainability. 20% External Relations, Donor Engagement and Positioning Enhanced organizational visibility, reputation, and influence among donors, government institutions, development partners, foundations, and private sector stakeholders. Strong donor retention, stewardship, and strategic partnerships that expand funding opportunities. Enhanced financial sustainability through diversified revenue streams and continuous improvement in resource mobilization performance. 5% Technical support, Mentorship and Talent Development A high-performing, skilled, and motivated Resource Mobilization team capable of delivering World Vision Rwanda's resource acquisition and growth objectives. Effective workforce planning, succession management, and staff development, ensuring continuity of critical resource mobilization capabilities and leadership pipeline development. Strong cross-functional collaboration and alignment across Programmes, Operations, Finance, Communications, Support Offices, and other stakeholders in support of resource acquisition goals. Compliance with organizational policies, standards, and regulatory requirements across the Resource Mobilization function. Successful delivery of special assignments and cross-organizational initiatives as delegated.
